name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship (NMMSS)
department: Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education
applyChannel: the National Scholarship Portal after clearing the state NMMS exam
description: Scholarship to reduce dropouts at Class 8 by supporting meritorious students from economically weaker sections through Class 9 to 12.
whoCanApply: Students in government / aided / local body schools who clear the state-level NMMS selection test, with parental income up to ₹3.5 lakh.
benefits: Direct financial assistance of ₹12,000 per year (₹1,000 per month) from Class 9 to Class 12 (total ₹48,000 over 4 years) transferred directly into the student's bank account via DBT on the National Scholarship Portal.
deadlineInfo: State exam held in November/December; NSP portal submission opens annually from July to November.

rules.label: Cleared the state NMMS selection exam and studies in a government/aided school

process: Step 1: When studying in Class 8, apply for the State NMMSS Examination through your school headmaster in August/September.
Step 2: Appear for the competitive exam consisting of MAT (Mental Ability Test) and SAT (Scholastic Aptitude Test) in November/December.
Step 3: State SCERT / Education Department publishes the Merit List of selected scholars.
Step 4: Selected students register on the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) under NMMSS.
Step 5: Fill in Student Profile, Class 8 school details, Aadhaar number, and Bank Account details.
Step 6: Upload Income Certificate, Caste Certificate, and Marksheet.
Step 7: Submit the application on NSP and submit a printed copy to your school principal.
Step 8: School verifies your enrollment on the portal (Level 1), and District Nodal Officer approves (Level 2).
Step 9: Ministry of Education transfers ₹12,000 per year directly to the student's bank account via PFMS.
Step 10: Apply for annual renewal on NSP in Classes 10, 11, and 12 upon passing previous year exams.

faqs.q: How many scholarships are available under NMMSS?
faqs.a: One lakh (1,00,000) fresh scholarships are awarded every year across all states and union territories in India.

faqs.q: What is the examination pattern for NMMSS?
faqs.a: The exam consists of two 90-minute tests: 1) Mental Ability Test (MAT) with 90 multiple-choice questions on reasoning, and 2) Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) with 90 questions covering science, mathematics, and social studies.

faqs.q: Can students of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (JNV) apply?
faqs.a: No. JNV, Kendriya Vidyalaya, and other fully subsidized residential school students are not eligible.

faqs.q: What happens if I score less than 55% in Class 9 or 10?
faqs.a: To continue receiving the scholarship in Classes 10, 11, and 12, you must secure at least 55% marks (50% for SC/ST) in the annual promotional examination.

faqs.q: Can I choose Science, Arts, or Commerce in Class 11 and keep the scholarship?
faqs.a: Yes. You can pursue any recognized stream in higher secondary education (Classes 11 and 12) in government or aided schools.

faqs.q: Is there an examination fee to appear for NMMSS?
faqs.a: States charge a nominal application fee of around ₹50 to ₹100, which is often waived or subsidized for SC/ST students.

purpose: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS), implemented by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to arrest dropouts at Class 8 and encourage them to complete secondary and higher secondary schooling up to Class 12.
targetBeneficiary: Students studying in Class 8 in government, local body, and government-aided schools who clear the statewide NMMSS selection examination.
financialBenefit: ₹12,000 per year (₹1,000 per month) from Class 9 through Class 12
benefitFrequency: Annual single lump-sum credit (₹12,000) for 4 consecutive years
impact: Prevents high school dropouts among talented rural and economically disadvantaged children, ensuring they pass Class 12.

detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Minimum 55% marks in Class 7 annual exam (50% for SC/ST students); enrolled in government, government-aided, or local body school.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (General, OBC, SC, ST) with applicable state reservation quotas.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Verified family annual income below ₹3.5 Lakh.

process: Step 1: Complete OTR (One-Time Registration) on scholarships.gov.in using Aadhaar.
Step 2: Log in and select 'Ministry of Minority Affairs' -> 'Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for Minorities'.
Step 3: Enter academic details, previous examination percentage (must be >= 50%), and current course.
Step 4: Select your religious community (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, or Parsi).
Step 5: Fill in family annual income and bank account details.
Step 6: Upload Marksheet, Income Certificate, Minority Community Declaration, and Fee Receipt.
Step 7: Submit the application and print the confirmation copy.
Step 8: Submit the printout and copies of documents to your college scholarship officer.
Step 9: College verifies (Level 1), District Minority Welfare Officer approves (Level 2).
Step 10: Funds are transferred directly to your bank account via PFMS.

faqs.q: Which communities are covered under this scheme?
faqs.a: Six notified minority communities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, and Parsis (Zoroastrians).

faqs.q: Is there a quota for female students?
faqs.a: Yes. 30% of all scholarships are earmarked exclusively for female students.

faqs.q: What is the minimum percentage required?
faqs.a: You must score at least 50% marks in the final examination of the preceding class.

faqs.q: Can Class 11 and 12 students apply?
faqs.a: Yes. The Post Matric scheme covers Class 11, Class 12, ITI, Polytechnic, Diploma, Undergraduate, Postgraduate, and Ph.D. courses.

faqs.q: What is the family income limit?
faqs.a: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹2,00,000 per annum.

faqs.q: Can I receive both a state minority scholarship and this central scholarship?
faqs.a: No. You can only avail one government scholarship at a time.

benefitFrequency: Annual single-year disbursement
impact: Closes the educational gap for religious minorities, promotes gender balance (30% earmarked for girls), and reduces dropout rates in higher secondary education.

process: Step 1: Secure admission to any of the 260+ premier institutions (e.g. IIT Bombay, IIM Ahmedabad, NLSIU Bengaluru, AIIMS New Delhi).
Step 2: Visit scholarships.gov.in and complete OTR registration.
Step 3: Select 'Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment' -> 'Top Class Education Scheme for SC Students'.
Step 4: Enter Institute AISHE code, course details, entrance exam rank, and roll number.
Step 5: Fill in family income and bank account details.
Step 6: Upload Caste certificate, Income certificate, Fee structure, and Admission letter.
Step 7: Submit online and submit a copy to the Institute Registrar / Scholarship Nodal Officer.
Step 8: Institute verifies student records on NSP portal (Level 1).
Step 9: Ministry of Social Justice approves the scholarship.
Step 10: Tuition fees are disbursed directly to the institute, and living/laptop allowances are credited to the student's bank account.

faqs.q: Which institutions are covered under the Top Class SC scheme?
faqs.a: Over 260+ institutions of national repute, including all IITs, IIMs, NITs, IIITs, AIIMS, National Law Universities (NLUs), NID, NIFT, and top NIRF-ranked private universities.

faqs.q: What is the income limit for Top Class SC scholarship?
faqs.a: The family annual income limit is ₹8,00,000 (Eight Lakh Rupees) per annum.

faqs.q: Is the full tuition fee paid by the government?
faqs.a: Yes. For government premier institutes (IITs/IIMs/NITs/AIIMS), 100% of the actual tuition fee is paid. For notified private institutes, fees up to ₹2.0 Lakh per year are covered.

faqs.q: How much is the laptop/computer grant?
faqs.a: A one-time grant of ₹45,000 is provided to purchase a laptop, desktop, or tablet with printer accessories.

faqs.q: What happens if a student fails a semester exam?
faqs.a: The scholarship continues for the normal duration of the course, but will not be paid for any repeated years or extended semesters.

faqs.q: Can a student apply in the 2nd year if they missed applying in 1st year?
faqs.a: Fresh applications are accepted primarily in the first year of the course. Renewal applications continue for subsequent years.

faqs.q: How many Pragati scholarships are awarded each year?
faqs.a: AICTE awards 10,000 scholarships annually (5,000 for Degree and 5,000 for Diploma), plus all eligible applicants from 23 special/NE states.

faqs.q: Can two sisters from the same family apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Up to two girl children from the same family are eligible to receive the Pragati scholarship.

faqs.q: What expenses can the ₹50,000 amount be used for?
faqs.a: The lump-sum amount of ₹50,000/year can be utilized towards college fees, purchase of computers, software, books, equipment, and competitive examination fees without itemized audit.

faqs.q: Can lateral entry students into 2nd year apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Female students admitted directly into the 2nd year of B.Tech through lateral entry counseling can apply.

faqs.q: What is the family income limit?
faqs.a: Total family annual income must not exceed ₹8,00,000 per annum.

faqs.q: Is there any reservation for SC/ST and OBC students in Pragati?
faqs.a: Yes, constitutional reservation applies: 15% for SC, 7.5% for ST, and 27% for OBC candidates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum disability percentage required?

faqs.q: Can I use the scholarship to buy a hearing aid or motorized wheelchair?
faqs.a: Yes, the ₹50,000/year assistance can be freely utilized towards purchase of assistive devices, laptops, software, and college fees.

faqs.q: Can male students apply for Saksham?

faqs.q: What is the family income limit?

name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
applyChannel: any bank branch or Business Correspondent (Bank Mitra)
description: Zero-balance basic savings bank account for every unbanked adult — the gateway to DBT, insurance and pension schemes.
whoCanApply: Any Indian citizen without a bank account (minors aged 10+ can open with a guardian).
benefits: Zero-balance Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) account with no minimum balance penalty + Free RuPay Debit Card with built-in ₹2,00,000 accidental insurance coverage (₹1 Lakh for accounts opened before Aug 2018) + ₹10,000 Overdraft (OD) credit facility per eligible household + Direct platform for all central and state DBT subsidies.
deadlineInfo: Permanent national financial inclusion mission open year-round.

process: Step 1: Walk into any public sector bank, private bank, Gramin bank, or neighborhood Bank Mitra kiosk.
Step 2: Collect the free PMJDY Account Opening Form (available in Hindi, English, and regional languages).
Step 3: Fill in your Name, Date of Birth, Aadhaar Number, Mobile Number, and Nominee details.
Step 4: Attach a photocopy of your Aadhaar Card and 2 passport photos.
Step 5: Perform biometric fingerprint authentication on the micro-ATM terminal.
Step 6: Account is generated with zero opening deposit requirement.
Step 7: Collect your free Jan Dhan Passbook on the spot.
Step 8: Within 7 to 10 days, receive your free RuPay Debit Card with ₹2,00,000 accident insurance.
Step 9: Operate the account regularly for 6 months to unlock the ₹10,000 Overdraft facility.

faqs.q: Is any minimum balance required to maintain a Jan Dhan account?
faqs.a: No! PMJDY accounts are 100% Zero-Balance accounts. There is absolutely NO minimum balance requirement, and banks cannot deduct any penalty even if the balance is ₹0.00.

faqs.q: What is the RuPay Card Accidental Insurance amount?
faqs.a: For PMJDY accounts opened after 28 August 2018, the RuPay debit card carries a free accidental death and disability insurance cover of ₹2,00,000 (Two Lakh Rupees).

faqs.q: What is the ₹10,000 Overdraft facility?
faqs.a: After 6 months of satisfactory account operation, account holders can withdraw up to ₹10,000 even if their account balance is zero, providing emergency credit without collateral.

faqs.q: Can I receive all government subsidies in my Jan Dhan account?
faqs.a: Yes! PMJDY accounts are automatically enabled for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and receive subsidies for PM-KISAN, Ujjwala, scholarships, and pensions.

faqs.q: Can children open a Jan Dhan account?
faqs.a: Any child aged 10 years and above can open a Jan Dhan savings account operated independently or jointly with parents.

faqs.q: Can I transfer money using UPI from a Jan Dhan account?
faqs.a: Yes! You can link your PMJDY RuPay debit card to BHIM, Google Pay, PhonePe, or Paytm for instant digital payments.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, is the world's largest financial inclusion mission, ensuring that every unbanked household in India has access to formal banking services, basic savings accounts, affordable credit, insurance, and direct government DBT transfers.

financialBenefit: Zero-balance bank account + ₹2,00,000 free accidental insurance + ₹10,000 overdraft facility
benefitFrequency: Permanent banking account with active transactional privileges
impact: Has opened over 53 crore bank accounts holding over ₹2.3 lakh crore in savings, with over 55% accounts owned by women and 67% in rural areas, ending financial exclusion in India.

detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Overdraft facility up to ₹10,000 granted to one person per household (preferably the female head).

department: Ministry of Labour & Employment

benefits: Free 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) e-Shram Card with nationwide portability. Free accidental death and permanent disability insurance cover of ₹2,00,000 (and ₹1,00,000 for partial disability) under PMSBY. Seamless delivery of emergency relief during natural disasters/pandemics, and direct integration with central/state pension and skill upgrading portals.

process: Step 1: Visit the official portal eshram.gov.in and click 'Register on e-Shram'.
Step 2: Enter your Aadhaar-linked Mobile Number and Captcha; verify via OTP.
Step 3: Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar Number and perform Aadhaar OTP authentication (or fingerprint at CSC).
Step 4: Personal details (Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Address) are automatically fetched from the Aadhaar database.
Step 5: Fill in additional details: Marital status, Social Category, Blood Group, and Nominee details.
Step 6: Enter your Occupation & Skill (Select primary occupation from the National Classification of Occupations list).
Step 7: Provide Bank Account details (Bank Name, Account Number, IFSC).
Step 8: Review the preview of your self-declaration.
Step 9: Submit the registration. Your 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) is generated immediately.
Step 10: Download and print your full-color e-Shram UAN Card.

faqs.q: What is an e-Shram UAN Card?
faqs.a: The e-Shram Card is a laminated card with a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) that serves as universal proof of registration in India's National Database of Unorganised Workers.

faqs.q: Is there any fee to register for e-Shram at a CSC?
faqs.a: No! Registration for e-Shram is 100% FREE across India. The Ministry of Labour pays the CSC commission directly.

faqs.q: Does the e-Shram card provide accidental insurance?
faqs.a: Yes, registered e-Shram workers receive accidental death and permanent total disability insurance cover of ₹2,00,000 (and ₹1,00,000 for partial disability).

faqs.q: Can gig workers (Zomato, Swiggy, Uber, Ola delivery partners) register?
faqs.a: Yes! Platform and gig workers are officially categorized under e-Shram and are strongly encouraged to register.

faqs.q: Can agricultural laborers and farmers register?
faqs.a: Agricultural workers and landless farm laborers who do not pay income tax are fully eligible.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay any monthly contribution to keep the card active?
faqs.a: No! Unlike pension schemes, e-Shram is a registry card and requires ZERO monthly contributions.

purpose: The e-Shram Portal, developed by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is India's first national centralized database of unorganized workers, delivering a Universal Account Number (UAN) card that integrates informal workers with national social security schemes, accident insurance, and emergency disaster relief.
targetBeneficiary: All unorganized workers aged 16 to 59 years (construction workers, migrant workers, street vendors, domestic workers, agricultural laborers, gig and platform workers, auto drivers, fishermen, and brick kiln workers).
financialBenefit: Universal Account Number (UAN) e-Shram Card + ₹2,00,000 accidental insurance coverage + priority social security access
benefitFrequency: Permanent digital card with active national database registration
impact: Brings over 30 crore informal workers out of invisibility, providing a single digital identity for targeted DBT welfare benefits, ration portability, and social security.

name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM)
department: Ministry of Labour & Employment
applyChannel: a Common Service Centre or the Maandhan portal
description: Voluntary contributory pension scheme for unorganised workers, with matching government contribution.
whoCanApply: Unorganised workers aged 18–40 with monthly income up to ₹15,000, not EPFO/ESIC/NPS members and not income-tax payers.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹3,000 per month starting from age 60 until death. 50:50 matching contribution: the worker contributes a modest ₹55 to ₹200 per month (depending on entry age), and the Central Government deposits the exact same matching amount into the pension fund. Family pension: upon subscriber's death, spouse receives 50% of the pension (₹1,500/month) for life.
deadlineInfo: Can be joined anytime between ages 18 and 40. Open year-round.

process: Step 1: Visit any Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar card and Bank Passbook.
Step 2: CSC operator enters your Aadhaar number and Mobile number on maandhan.in.
Step 3: Perform biometric fingerprint authentication.
Step 4: Enter Occupation, Monthly Income (<= ₹15,000), and Nominee details.
Step 5: System calculates monthly contribution based on age (e.g. ₹55/month at age 18; ₹100/month at age 29; ₹200/month at age 40).
Step 6: Pay the 1st month's contribution in cash to the CSC operator.
Step 7: Sign the auto-debit mandate form, which the operator scans and uploads.
Step 8: Your unique PM-SYM Pension Card is printed and handed over on the spot.
Step 9: Subsequent monthly contributions are automatically debited from your bank account until age 60.
Step 10: Upon turning 60, guaranteed monthly pension of ₹3,000 starts flowing into your bank account.

faqs.q: How much does the government contribute to my PM-SYM account?
faqs.a: The Government of India contributes an exact matching 50% amount. For example, if you contribute ₹100 per month, the Central Government deposits an additional ₹100 per month into your pension account.

faqs.q: What happens if a subscriber dies before age 60?
faqs.a: If the subscriber passes away before age 60, the spouse can either continue the scheme by paying regular contributions or exit the scheme and receive the entire accumulated corpus with bank interest.

faqs.q: What happens if the pensioner dies after age 60?
faqs.a: Upon the pensioner's death, the spouse is entitled to receive 50% of the pension (₹1,500 per month) as a lifelong family pension.

faqs.q: Can a domestic maid or construction worker join?
faqs.a: Yes! PM-SYM is tailor-made for unorganized workers like domestic helpers, street vendors, rickshaw pullers, cobblers, and agricultural workers.

faqs.q: Can I leave the scheme before 60 years?
faqs.a: Yes, voluntary exit is permitted. If you exit within 10 years, you receive back your entire contribution with savings bank interest.

faqs.q: What is the monthly contribution at age 18 vs age 40?
faqs.a: At age 18, you pay only ₹55 per month; at age 29, you pay ₹100 per month; at the maximum entry age of 40, you pay ₹200 per month.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM), launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme that provides assured social security of ₹3,00,000 per year (₹3,000/month) to unorganized workers in their old age, backed by an equal 50:50 matching contribution from the Central Government.
targetBeneficiary: Unorganized workers aged 18 to 40 years whose monthly income is ₹15,000 or less.
financialBenefit: Guaranteed lifetime pension of ₹3,000 per month from age 60 + 50% family pension for spouse
benefitFrequency: Monthly guaranteed pension for lifetime from age 60
impact: Builds a formal pension safety net for informal domestic maids, street vendors, rickshaw pullers, construction workers, and agricultural laborers.

name: PM Vishwakarma
department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
description: End-to-end support for traditional artisans and craftspeople in 18 trades such as carpentry, pottery, tailoring and smithing.
whoCanApply: Artisans aged 18+ working with hands and tools in one of the 18 listed family-based trades (one member per family).
benefits: Recognition as Vishwakarma through PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card + Free Basic Skill Training (5–7 days) with a stipend of ₹500 per day + Advanced Skill Training (15 days) + ₹15,000 Modern Tool-kit Incentive Grant + Collateral-free enterprise credit up to ₹3,00,000 (Tranche 1: ₹1,00,000 at 5% interest; Tranche 2: ₹2,00,000 at 5% interest) with 8% interest subvention by the Central Government.
estimatedBenefit: Training, toolkit support and concessional credit
occupationRequirement: Traditional artisan in a listed trade
deadlineInfo: Comprehensive 5-year central scheme running through 2028. Open year-round.

process: Step 1: Visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar card and Bank Passbook.
Step 2: CSC operator logs into pmvishwakarma.gov.in and completes biometric Aadhaar authentication.
Step 3: Select your trade from the 18 notified traditional trades (e.g. Carpenter, Tailor, Barber, Mason, Blacksmith).
Step 4: Enter family details from Ration card and bank account details.

Step 5: Submit application online. A 3-tier verification begins: Gram Panchayat Head / ULB Executive verifies (Level 1); District Implementation Committee verifies (Level 2); Screening Committee approves (Level 3).
Step 6: Download your digital PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card.
Step 7: Attend 5 to 7 days Basic Skill Training at the local training centre (receive ₹500/day stipend).
Step 8: Receive an e-RUPI / e-voucher of ₹15,000 on your mobile phone to purchase modern specialized tool-kits.
Step 9: Eligible artisans can apply for the 1st Tranche collateral-free loan of ₹1,00,000 at 5% interest.
Step 10: Repay regular installments over 18 months to unlock the 2nd Tranche loan of ₹2,00,000 (30 months repayment).

faqs.q: Which 18 trades are covered under PM Vishwakarma?
faqs.a: 1) Carpenter (Suthar), 2) Boat Maker, 3) Armourer, 4) Blacksmith (Lohar), 5) Hammer & Tool Kit Maker, 6) Locksmith, 7) Sculptor (Moortikar/Stone carver), 8) Goldsmith (Sonar), 9) Potter (Kumhaar), 10) Cobbler (Charmakar), 11) Mason (Rajmistri), 12) Basket/Mat/Broom Maker/Coir weaver, 13) Doll & Toy Maker (Traditional), 14) Barber (Naai), 15) Garland Maker (Malakaar), 16) Washerman (Dhobi), 17) Tailor (Darzi), and 18) Fishing Net Maker.

faqs.q: Is the ₹15,000 tool-kit grant a loan that I have to repay?
faqs.a: No! The ₹15,000 tool-kit grant is a 100% FREE incentive provided by the Central Government to purchase modern tools; you do not have to repay a single rupee.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on the PM Vishwakarma loan?
faqs.a: The interest rate charged to the artisan is fixed at a deeply subsidized 5% per annum. The remaining interest is directly subvented by the Government of India (up to 8%).

faqs.q: Do I have to pay any fee at the CSC for registration?
faqs.a: No! Registration for PM Vishwakarma at all Common Service Centres is completely FREE. The Government of India pays the CSC fee directly.

faqs.q: Do I get paid while attending the training?
faqs.a: Yes! Every artisan receives a daily training stipend of ₹500 per day for the entire 5 to 7 days of basic training, transferred directly to their bank account.

faqs.q: Is collateral required for the ₹1 Lakh and ₹2 Lakh loans?
faqs.a: No collateral or third-party guarantee is required. The loans are 100% credit guaranteed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC).

purpose: PM Vishwakarma, launched by the Ministry of MSME, is an historic national initiative designed to provide end-to-end holistic institutional support to traditional artisans and craftspeople who work with their hands and tools, preserving ancient Indian craftsmanship, modernizing tools, providing skills training, and linking artisans with domestic and global markets.
targetBeneficiary: Artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades (Carpenters, Blacksmiths, Goldsmiths, Potters, Sculptors, Cobblers, Masons, Basket/Mat/Broom makers, Doll & Toy makers, Barbers, Garland makers, Washermen, Tailors, Fishing Net makers, etc.).
financialBenefit: ₹15,00,000 free toolkit grant + ₹500/day training stipend + ₹3,00,000 collateral-free loan at 5% subsidized interest
benefitFrequency: One-time toolkit grant + continuous skill development and enterprise loan tranches
impact: Elevates traditional informal artisans into recognized micro-entrepreneurs, upgrades handmade product quality with modern power tools, and integrates village crafts into formal supply chains and e-commerce.

detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Only one member per family (husband, wife, and minor children) can receive benefits under the scheme.

commonMistakes: Family member already enrolled: The scheme strictly limits benefits to ONE person per family.
Attempting to cash out the ₹15,000 tool-kit voucher: The ₹15,000 is issued as a targeted e-RUPI digital voucher that can ONLY be redeemed at registered tool equipment merchants.
Missing the basic training: Loan and tool-kit grants are unlocked only after finishing the 5-day training.
processingTime: Level 1 to Level 3 verification completed within 30 to 45 days.
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; certificate and ID card are valid for life.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on pmvishwakarma.gov.in using Aadhaar number and OTP.

disbursementDetails: Training stipend (₹500/day) is credited directly to the artisan's bank account. The ₹15,000 tool-kit incentive is delivered as an e-RUPI QR voucher to the mobile phone. Enterprise loans (up to ₹3 Lakh) are disbursed by banks at 5% interest.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
applyChannel: banks, NBFCs, MFIs or the Udyamimitra portal
description: Collateral-free loans for non-farm micro and small enterprises in manufacturing, trading and services.

No processing fees for Shishu loans.

documents.issuingAuthority: Prepared by entrepreneur / chartered accountant / equipment vendor
documents.format: Written project report + vendor quotation for machinery

documents.name: Passport Size Photographs
documents.why: Loan file and Mudra Card generation.

process: Step 1: Prepare your business plan and machinery quotations (if purchasing equipment).
Step 2: Visit jansamarth.in or udyamimitra.in, or walk into your nearest commercial/Gramin bank branch.
Step 3: Register and select 'Business Activity Loan' -> 'Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana'.
Step 4: Choose your loan tier: Shishu (up to ₹50K), Kishore (₹50K–₹5L), or Tarun (₹5L–₹20L).
Step 5: Fill in Personal Details, Udyam Number, Business Nature, and Projected Sales.
Step 6: Upload PAN Card, Aadhaar, Bank Statement, and Machinery Quotations.
Step 7: The portal matches your proposal with multiple lenders (SBI, PNB, Canara, Bank of Baroda, NBFCs, etc.).
Step 8: Selected bank reviews the application and conducts a brief field inspection of your shop/factory.
Step 9: Bank sanctions the loan and issues the Sanction Letter.
Step 10: Term loan is disbursed directly to the machinery vendor, and working capital is credited to a MUDRA RuPay Debit Card account.

faqs.q: What is the new maximum loan limit under MUDRA?
faqs.a: In Union Budget 2024, the central government created a new 'Tarun Plus' category, raising the maximum MUDRA loan ceiling from ₹10 Lakh to ₹20,00,000 for entrepreneurs who have previously taken and successfully repaid Tarun loans.

faqs.q: Do I have to pledge any property or land as security?
faqs.a: No! All MUDRA loans are 100% collateral-free and third-party guarantee-free. Loans are backed by the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) managed by NCGTC.

faqs.q: What are the 4 categories of MUDRA loans?
faqs.a: 1) Shishu: up to ₹50,000; 2) Kishore: above ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000; 3) Tarun: above ₹5,00,000 to ₹10,00,000; 4) Tarun Plus: above ₹10,00,000 to ₹20,00,000.

faqs.q: What is a MUDRA Card?
faqs.a: A MUDRA Card is a RuPay debit card linked to your working capital cash credit account, allowing you to withdraw money as needed and pay interest only on the utilized amount.

faqs.q: Can a vegetable vendor, tailor, or tea stall owner apply?
faqs.a: Yes! MUDRA was created specifically for micro-enterprises like tea stalls, tailoring units, kirana stores, beauty salons, and artisan workshops.

faqs.q: What should I do if a bank manager refuses to accept my MUDRA form?
faqs.a: Escalate to the Bank's Lead District Manager (LDM), call the State MUDRA Nodal Helpline, or lodge a formal complaint on the JanSamarth portal or RBI CMS portal.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), launched by the Ministry of Finance, provides collateral-free institutional business loans up to ₹20,00,000 to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises, funding the unfunded and fueling grassroots entrepreneurship across India.
targetBeneficiary: Micro-entrepreneurs, small shopkeepers, artisans, street vendors, small manufacturing units, service sector enterprises, and allied agricultural business owners.
financialBenefit: Collateral-free business loans up to ₹20,00,000 (Shishu up to ₹50K, Kishore up to ₹5L, Tarun up to ₹10L, Tarun Plus up to ₹20L) with zero third-party guarantee
benefitFrequency: Term loan or overdraft working capital credit line (repayable over 3 to 7 years)
impact: Has sanctioned over 48 crore loans totaling more than ₹27 lakh crore across India, with over 68% of loans sanctioned to women entrepreneurs, generating massive self-employment in manufacturing, trading, and services.

detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: All genders eligible; special concessions and priority for women entrepreneurs under Mahila Udyami scheme.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling; loan eligibility is evaluated on business viability and cash flow.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: None for Shishu; basic literacy/technical knowledge for technical enterprises.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Micro-entrepreneurs, shopkeepers, fruit/vegetable sellers, artisans, transporters, small manufacturers, salon owners, and repair workshops.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (General, OBC, SC, ST, EWS).
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India residing in bank's operational area.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Individual, proprietorship, partnership, or private limited enterprise.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an Indian citizen with a viable non-farm business or allied agricultural project proposal
Must not be a defaulter on any previous loan with any bank or financial institution
Must possess valid identity and address proof (Aadhaar, PAN Card, Business Registration/Udyam if applicable)
conditionalRequirements: Udyam Registration Certificate and project report mandatory for loans exceeding ₹50,000 (Kishore and Tarun).
ineligibility: Large corporate houses or educational institutions
Direct crop cultivation (covered under Kisan Credit Card)
Willful defaulters with impaired CIBIL/credit records
Non-Indian citizens
applicationMode: Online via Udyamimitra Portal (udyamimitra.in) / JanSamarth Portal (jansamarth.in) or Offline at any Bank Branch
offlineProcess: Walk into any branch of a Public Sector Bank, Private Bank, Regional Rural Bank (RRB), or Small Finance Bank (SFB). Ask for the Mudra Loan Desk. Submit the standard Mudra loan application form with your KYC and business quotation.
commonMistakes: Banks asking for collateral: By law, MUDRA loans are 100% COLLATERAL-FREE; banks cannot demand mortgage of property or gold.
Applying without a clear business proposal: Stating a vague purpose leads to branch-level rejection; provide clear vendor quotations for machinery or stock.
Having unpaid credit card/personal loan defaults: A severely impaired CIBIL score halts institutional loan sanction.
processingTime: 7 to 14 working days for Shishu loans; 15 to 25 working days for Kishore/Tarun loans.
renewalRequired: Working capital overdraft renewed annually; term loans repayable over 36 to 84 months.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on jansamarth.in or udyamimitra.in using your Application Number.
correctionProcedure: Visit the lending bank branch to rectify missing documents or update project estimates.
disbursementMethod: Direct Disbursement to Equipment Vendor (Term Loan) & MUDRA RuPay Card (Working Capital)
disbursementDetails: For capital machinery, the bank pays the equipment supplier directly via RTGS/NEFT. For working capital, the borrower receives a MUDRA RuPay Debit Card to withdraw cash at ATMs or swipe for raw material purchases.

name: Stand-Up India
department: Department of Financial Services / SIDBI
applyChannel: the Stand-Up Mitra portal or any scheduled commercial bank branch
description: Bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs setting up a greenfield enterprise.
whoCanApply: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs aged 18+ setting up a new (greenfield) enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activities.
benefits: Composite bank loan (term loan + working capital) between ₹10,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000 covering up to 85% of total project cost. Margin money requirement is reduced to just 15% (which can be converged with eligible state/central subsidy schemes). No collateral required if covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand-Up India (CGFSI).
deadlineInfo: Union Government extended the Stand-Up India scheme through 2025; open year-round.

rules.label: Woman entrepreneur (or SC/ST — see indicator below)
Setting up a new greenfield enterprise; not a loan defaulter

documents.name: Caste Certificate (for SC/ST applicants)
documents.why: Proves constitutional category eligibility (not required for women of General/OBC).

documents.name: Aadhaar Card & PAN Card
documents.why: Identity, age, and individual KYC.

documents.name: Comprehensive Detailed Project Report (DPR)
documents.why: Explains business model, technical feasibility, market viability, financial projections, and payback schedule.
documents.issuingAuthority: Prepared by Chartered Accountant / Project Consultant / SIDBI Handholding Agency
documents.format: Bound project report with financial balance sheets and cash flows

documents.name: Rent Agreement / Lease Deed / Land Ownership of Factory Premises
documents.why: Confirms location and physical premises for the greenfield project.

documents.name: Machinery & Equipment Quotations from Vendors
documents.why: Validates capital expenditure requirement for term loan disbursement.

process: Step 1: Visit standupmitra.in and click 'Register as Entrepreneur'.
Step 2: Complete user registration and choose whether you need 'Handholding Support' (from SIDBI, NABARD, DIC) or are 'Ready to Apply'.
Step 3: Fill in Project Profile: Nature of Business (Manufacturing, Service, Trading, or Agri-Allied), Total Project Cost, and Desired Loan Amount.
Step 4: Upload PAN Card, Aadhaar, Caste Certificate (if SC/ST), Project Report, and Machinery Quotations.
Step 5: Select your preferred bank branch or choose automated allocation across scheduled commercial banks.
Step 6: Submit application online. An Application Reference Number is generated.
Step 7: Bank branch manager receives the file, examines the Detailed Project Report, and calls the entrepreneur for an interview.
Step 8: Bank conducts site inspection and approves the loan sanction under CGFSI guarantee.
Step 9: Entrepreneur deposits the 15% margin money; term loan is released directly to machinery vendors.
Step 10: Working capital limit is activated to commence commercial production.

faqs.q: What is the minimum and maximum loan amount under Stand-Up India?
faqs.a: The loan amount ranges from a minimum of ₹10,00,000 (Ten Lakh Rupees) up to a maximum of ₹1,00,00,000 (One Crore Rupees).

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for Stand-Up India?
faqs.a: SC entrepreneurs, ST entrepreneurs, and ALL Women entrepreneurs (including General, OBC, Minority, SC, and ST women) aged 18+ setting up a first-time greenfield business.

faqs.q: What is meant by a 'Greenfield' enterprise?
faqs.a: Greenfield enterprise means the first-time venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, trading, or agri-allied sectors.

faqs.q: How much margin money does the entrepreneur have to arrange?
faqs.a: Borrowers need to bring in only 15% margin money of the total project cost, which can also be converged with eligible central or state subsidy schemes.

faqs.q: What is the repayment tenure?
faqs.a: The loan is repayable in up to 7 years with an initial moratorium period of up to 18 months.

faqs.q: Can a partnership firm apply?
faqs.a: Yes, provided at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake is held by the SC, ST, or Woman entrepreneur.

purpose: The Stand-Up India Scheme, administered by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, promotes entrepreneurship among women and Scheduled Caste (SC) & Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities by facilitating bank loans between ₹10,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000 for setting up greenfield (first-time) enterprises in manufacturing, services, trading, or agri-allied sectors.
targetBeneficiary: SC, ST, and Women entrepreneurs setting up a greenfield enterprise (first-time venture).
financialBenefit: Bank credit between ₹10,00,000 and ₹1,00,00,000 covering up to 85% of greenfield project cost
benefitFrequency: Composite term loan + working capital facility repayable over up to 7 years with 18-month moratorium
impact: Creates institutional wealth and high-value business ownership among historically under-represented communities, transforming job seekers into major job creators.

detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Women of any category, OR male/female entrepreneurs belonging to SC or ST communities.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: None mandated; entrepreneurial capability assessed on project feasibility.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: SC, ST, or Women of all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: In non-individual enterprises, at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC, ST, or Woman entrepreneur.

mandatoryConditions: Borrower must be an SC, ST, or Woman entrepreneur aged 18 years or older
The venture must be a 'Greenfield' project (first-time venture in manufacturing, services, trading, or agri-allied sector)
Borrower must not be in default to any bank or financial institution
Borrower contribution (margin money) must be at least 15% of project cost (inclusive of state subsidies)
conditionalRequirements: In private limited companies or LLPs, 51%+ shareholding must be in the hands of the eligible SC/ST/Woman promoter.
ineligibility: Existing brownfield businesses seeking expansion (scheme is strictly for first-time greenfield ventures)
Male entrepreneurs belonging to General or OBC categories (unless entering as minority partner under 49% with SC/ST/Woman as 51%+ lead)
Willful loan defaulters
applicationMode: Online via Stand-Up Mitra Portal (standupmitra.in) or In-person at any Commercial Bank branch
offlineProcess: Every scheduled commercial bank branch in India is mandated under government directives to facilitate at least one SC/ST borrower and at least one Woman borrower under Stand-Up India. Walk into any bank branch and request the Branch Manager directly for Stand-Up India facilitation.
commonMistakes: Applying for existing business expansion: Stand-Up India strictly finances 'Greenfield' (first-time) ventures; existing units are directed to normal MSME schemes.
Submitting an incomplete Project Report: A professional Detailed Project Report (DPR) detailing break-even analysis is essential for loans between ₹10L and ₹1 Crore.
processingTime: Sanctioned within 30 to 45 working days following DPR scrutiny and interview.
renewalRequired: Term loan repayable over up to 7 years with up to 18 months moratorium; working capital reviewed annually.
trackingProcedure: Track application progress on standupmitra.in using your login credentials.
correctionProcedure: Handholding agencies (SIDBI/NABARD) assist with refining project reports if rejected by banks.
disbursementMethod: Direct RTGS/NEFT to Machinery Vendors (Term Loan) & Overdraft Facility (Working Capital)
disbursementDetails: Term loan component is disbursed directly into verified bank accounts of equipment manufacturers upon submission of purchase orders. Working capital is disbursed into the enterprise current account.

name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
department: KVIC, Ministry of MSME
description: Credit-linked subsidy for setting up new micro enterprises in rural and urban areas.
whoCanApply: Individuals aged 18+; Class 8 pass required for larger manufacturing/service projects. Only new projects qualify.
benefits: Substantial non-refundable government capital subsidy: 35% subsidy for Special Categories (SC, ST, OBC, Women, Minorities, Ex-Servicemen, Differently Abled) in rural areas; 25% subsidy for Special Categories in urban areas. General category beneficiaries receive 25% subsidy in rural areas and 15% in urban areas. Maximum project cost is ₹50,00,000 for Manufacturing and ₹20,00,000 for Service sector units.
deadlineInfo: Continuous national program. Applications processed in monthly agency batches year-round.

rules.label: Some formal education (Class 8 pass needed for larger projects)
Proposing a new project; not already availing other government subsidy for it

documents.name: Aadhaar Card & PAN Card
documents.why: Identity, age, and individual KYC.

documents.name: Detailed Project Report (DPR)
documents.why: Outlines capital expenditure (machinery), working capital requirement, sales projections, and employment potential.

documents.name: Caste / Special Category Certificate (if claiming 25%–35% subsidy)
documents.why: Confirms eligibility for higher special subsidy rate.

documents.name: Educational Qualification Certificate (Class 8 Marksheet or higher)
documents.why: Mandatory if project cost exceeds ₹10L (Mfg) or ₹5L (Services).

documents.name: Rural Area Certificate
documents.why: Confirms project location is in rural territory to claim the higher 35% subsidy rate.
documents.issuingAuthority: Gram Panchayat Secretary / Block Development Officer

process: Step 1: Visit kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal and click 'Application for New Unit'.
Step 2: Enter Aadhaar Number, Name, Sponsoring Agency (KVIC, KVIB, or DIC), and Project Location (Rural or Urban).
Step 3: Select Social Category (SC/ST/OBC/Woman/General) to determine your eligible subsidy percentage (15% to 35%).
Step 4: Enter Education qualification, Project cost breakdown (Capital Expenditure + Working Capital), and choose Financing Bank.
Step 5: Upload Project Report (DPR), Aadhaar, Caste certificate, Photo, and Rural certificate.
Step 6: Submit online. An Application Reference ID is generated immediately.
Step 7: Sponsoring agency (DIC/KVIC) screens application and forwards it electronically to your selected bank.
Step 8: Bank examines credit viability, conducts site inspection, and issues loan sanction letter.
Step 9: Complete mandatory 5 to 10 days Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training (online or offline).

Step 10: Bank releases first loan installment; KVIC deposits the Margin Money (subsidy) into a Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) in your bank account, which is adjusted after 3 years of successful operation.

faqs.q: What is the maximum subsidy under PMEGP?
faqs.a: For a Special Category entrepreneur (Woman, SC, ST, OBC, Minority) starting a manufacturing unit in a rural area, the government provides 35% subsidy on project costs up to ₹50 Lakh, which amounts to up to ₹17,50,000 in free government subsidy.

faqs.q: What is the maximum project cost allowed?
faqs.a: The maximum project cost is ₹50,00,000 (Fifty Lakh Rupees) for manufacturing enterprises and ₹20,00,000 (Twenty Lakh Rupees) for service/business enterprises.

faqs.q: How much own contribution does the applicant need to invest?
faqs.a: Special category entrepreneurs (including all women) invest only 5% of the project cost from their own pocket; General category entrepreneurs invest 10%.

faqs.q: What is EDP training under PMEGP?
faqs.a: Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) is a mandatory 5 to 10-day training covering business management, accounting, marketing, and taxation, which can be completed online via the PMEGP e-learning portal.

faqs.q: Can an existing business get a PMEGP loan?
faqs.a: The first PMEGP loan is strictly for new ventures. However, existing PMEGP units that have repaid their first loan successfully and achieved profit can apply for a Second Loan of up to ₹1 Crore for expansion with 15% subsidy.

faqs.q: Is collateral required for PMEGP loans?
faqs.a: Under RBI guidelines, no collateral security is required for PMEGP loans up to ₹10 Lakh. Loans between ₹10L and ₹50L are covered under the CGTMSE credit guarantee scheme without third-party guarantee.

purpose: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), administered by the Ministry of MSME through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), is a major credit-linked capital subsidy scheme designed to generate sustainable non-farm self-employment opportunities by financing new micro-enterprises across India.
targetBeneficiary: Individual entrepreneurs, Self-Help Groups (SHGs), cooperative societies, and trusts seeking to establish new micro-enterprises in manufacturing or service sectors.
financialBenefit: Government subsidy of 15% to 35% on project cost (Up to ₹17.5 Lakh subsidy for Manufacturing; up to ₹7.0 Lakh subsidy for Services)
benefitFrequency: One-time capital margin money subsidy locked in bank TDR for 3 years, then credited against loan
impact: Has established over 9 lakh micro-enterprises and generated more than 75 lakh jobs across rural and semi-urban India, creating small food processing factories, garment manufacturing units, and repair service centers.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 18 years and above (no upper age limit).
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: All genders eligible; women classified as Special Category eligible for 35% rural subsidy.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Class 8 pass mandatory for projects costing above ₹10 Lakh in manufacturing and above ₹5 Lakh in services; no educational qualification required below these thresholds.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Aspiring entrepreneur starting a new micro-enterprise.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (SC, ST, OBC, Minorities receive higher 35% rural subsidy).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Only one person per family can receive PMEGP assistance.

mandatoryConditions: Applicant must be an Indian citizen aged 18 years or older
Project must be a NEW enterprise (existing units cannot apply for 1st loan)
Applicant must contribute 5% (Special Category) or 10% (General Category) of project cost from own resources
Must undergo mandatory Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training before final subsidy release
Must pass Class 8 if project exceeds ₹10 Lakh (Manufacturing) or ₹5 Lakh (Services)
conditionalRequirements: Second loan up to ₹1 Crore available for upgrading high-performing existing PMEGP units with 15% subsidy.
ineligibility: Units involved in production/processing of meat, slaughterhouses, intoxicant liquor, tobacco products (bidi, pan, cigar)
Units manufacturing polythene carry bags of thickness less than statutory norms
Rural transport vehicles (except three-wheelers in Andaman/NE)
Existing units that have already availed government capital subsidy under another scheme
applicationMode: Online via PMEGP e-Portal (kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal)
offlineProcess: Entrepreneurs can visit their District Industries Centre (DIC) at the district headquarters, or the state Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) office. Officers help applicants prepare project reports and submit the online application.
commonMistakes: Applying for negative list industries: Projects involving tobacco, alcohol, poultry meat processing, or thin plastic bags are strictly prohibited.
Not completing EDP training: The subsidy (Margin Money) cannot be credited by KVIC until the entrepreneur finishes the online/offline EDP training.
Claiming rural subsidy for urban location: Location is verified by GPS; claiming rural rates for municipal areas causes rejection.
processingTime: Sanctioned within 45 to 60 days following bank and agency review.
renewalRequired: One-time setup subsidy; successful entrepreneurs can apply for a Second Loan up to ₹1 Crore after 3 years.
trackingProcedure: Track application progress on kviconline.gov.in using Application ID and Password.
correctionProcedure: District Task Force Committee / Bank allows re-upload of modified project reports if returned.
disbursementMethod: Direct Bank Loan + Government Margin Money Subsidy Credited to 3-Year Locked TDR Account
disbursementDetails: The bank finances the project via Term Loan and Working Capital. The government subsidy (15% to 35%) is credited into a separate interest-free Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) in the entrepreneur's name. After 3 years of successful enterprise inspection, the subsidy is credited against the loan principal.

name: National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)
department: Ministry of Education
description: Paid one-year apprenticeships for fresh graduates and diploma holders in industry.
whoCanApply: Graduates and diploma holders in engineering, general streams or vocational courses, usually within a few years of passing.
benefits: One year of structured on-the-job industrial apprenticeship in top public and private enterprises (BHEL, L&T, Tata, Infosys, BSNL, etc.) + Guaranteed monthly stipend: minimum ₹9,000 per month for Graduate Apprentices, ₹8,000 per month for Technician (Diploma) Apprentices, and ₹9,000 per month for General Stream Degree Apprentices (with 50% reimbursed by Central Government via DBT) + National Apprenticeship Certificate.
deadlineInfo: Continuous national portal open year-round; companies post fresh vacancies daily.

rules.label: Holds (or is completing) a diploma or degree
Passed out within the period allowed by NATS

documents.name: Provisional Degree / Diploma Certificate or Final Consolidated Marksheet
documents.why: Proves graduation from recognized university/board within last 3 years.
documents.issuingAuthority: University Registrar / State Board of Technical Education

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Identity verification and DBT stipend transfer.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Seeded Bank Passbook Copy
documents.why: For receiving central government share of monthly stipend via DBT.
documents.format: Passbook copy showing Account Number and IFSC

documents.name: Resume / Bio-Data
documents.why: For corporate employer evaluation during contract placement.

process: Step 1: Visit the modernized NATS 2.0 portal at nats.education.gov.in.
Step 2: Click 'Student' -> 'Student Register' and verify your Aadhaar via OTP.
Step 3: Enter educational qualification details: University/Board, College Name, Degree/Diploma, Passing Year, and Percentage.
Step 4: Upload Degree Certificate / Marksheet and Bank Passbook.
Step 5: Submit profile. The regional Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT) verifies and issues your Student NATS Enrollment Number.
Step 6: Log in and click 'Establishment Requests' -> 'Find Establishment' to search active apprenticeship vacancies by company, industry, or state.
Step 7: Apply to corporate establishments (e.g. BHEL, IOCL, L&T, DRDO, TCS).
Step 8: Company shortlists candidates and conducts interview or merit selection.
Step 9: Sign the online Apprenticeship Contract on the NATS portal.
Step 10: Undergo 1-year on-the-job training and receive minimum ₹8,000–₹9,000/month stipend via DBT. Upon completion, receive the Certificate of Proficiency.

faqs.q: What is the minimum monthly stipend under NATS?
faqs.a: The statutory minimum monthly stipend is ₹9,000/month for Graduate Apprentices (B.E./B.Tech and B.A./B.Sc./B.Com), and ₹8,000/month for Technician (Diploma) Apprentices. Many leading corporations pay higher stipends (₹15,000–₹25,000/month).

faqs.q: Can non-engineering general stream graduates (B.Com, B.Sc., B.A.) apply?
faqs.a: Yes! In 2021, the Cabinet expanded NATS to cover general stream graduates (B.A., B.Sc., B.Com, BBA, BCA) in sectors like retail, banking, logistics, and healthcare.

faqs.q: What is the maximum time gap after graduation to apply?
faqs.a: You must apply within 3 years of passing your qualifying degree or diploma examination.

faqs.q: What is the Certificate of Proficiency issued after 1 year?
faqs.a: The Certificate of Proficiency is an official national certificate issued by the Ministry of Education that is recognized globally as 1 year of valid work experience.

faqs.q: Does an apprenticeship guarantee a permanent job?
faqs.a: While an apprenticeship is a training contract, over 40% of high-performing apprentices are absorbed directly into permanent employment by their host companies.

faqs.q: Is there any exam to join NATS?
faqs.a: No national exam is conducted; companies shortlist candidates based on college marks or direct interviews.

purpose: National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS), implemented by the Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT/BOPT) under the Ministry of Education, bridges the campus-to-corporate skills gap by providing 1 year of hands-on practical industry training to fresh engineering, diploma, and general stream graduates with government-funded monthly stipends.
targetBeneficiary: Fresh graduates and diploma holders in Engineering, Technology, Architecture, Pharmacy, Hotel Management, and General Streams (B.A., B.Sc., B.Com, BBA, BCA) who passed within the last 3 years.
financialBenefit: Guaranteed monthly stipend of ₹8,000 to ₹9,000+ per month for 12 months + Certificate of Proficiency
benefitFrequency: Monthly stipend transfer throughout 1-year apprenticeship tenure
impact: Transforms theoretical college education into practical industry expertise, enhances employability, and leads to direct permanent corporate absorption for over 40% of apprentices.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Minimum 18 years of age (no upper age limit).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Graduate Degree (Engineering, Technology, General Streams: B.A., B.Sc., B.Com, BBA, BCA) or Diploma from a recognized university/technical board passed within the last 3 years.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Fresh graduate / job seeker seeking industrial training.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (General, OBC, SC, ST, EWS).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Individual student applicant.

mandatoryConditions: Must have completed an approved degree or diploma course from a recognized university or technical education board
Application must be filed within 3 years of passing the qualifying examination
Must NOT have undergone previous apprenticeship training under NATS elsewhere
Must NOT have 1 year or more of prior regular work experience
conditionalRequirements: Aadhaar-seeded bank account mandatory for receiving central government direct stipend reimbursement.
ineligibility: Candidates who passed their degree/diploma more than 3 years ago
Candidates who already have 1 year or more of regular full-time post-qualification work experience
Candidates who have already completed an apprenticeship under NATS or NAPS
applicationMode: Online via NATS 2.0 National Portal (nats.education.gov.in)
offlineProcess: Attend centralized Apprenticeship Mela (Job Fairs) organized periodically by BOAT/BOPT at technical colleges and government polytechnics across major cities.
commonMistakes: Passing year exceeding 3 years: The portal automatically checks graduation year and blocks students who graduated more than 3 years ago.
Bank account not mapped on NPCI: Since 50% of the stipend is paid by the Government of India via DBT, an unlinked bank account delays stipend credits.
processingTime: Student profile approved within 3 to 5 working days by regional BOAT.
renewalRequired: Apprenticeship contract is valid for strictly 12 months; cannot be repeated.
trackingProcedure: Track application and interview invitations on nats.education.gov.in dashboard.
correctionProcedure: Student can edit profile before signing the digital apprenticeship contract.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Student's Bank Account + Corporate Employer Transfer
disbursementDetails: Employer pays their share of the monthly stipend, and the Central Government reimburses its 50% share (up to ₹4,500/month) directly into the student's bank account via PFMS.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / NABARD
applyChannel: any bank branch (form also available on the PM-KISAN portal)
description: Short-term credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest and allied activities at concessional interest.
whoCanApply: Farmers — owner cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, SHGs and joint liability groups; also animal husbandry and fisheries farmers.
benefits: Revolving credit facility up to ₹3,00,000 at a deeply subsidized base interest rate of 7%. Farmers who repay on time receive an additional 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) from the central government, reducing the effective interest rate to just 4% per annum. Collateral-free credit limit up to ₹1,60,000.
deadlineInfo: Open throughout the year. Farmers can apply anytime at bank branches.

rules.label: Is a farmer (owner, tenant or sharecropper)

documents.format: Certified Revenue Extract / Online digitally signed copy

documents.why: Primary identity and address verification.

documents.why: Standard simplified loan application under the PM-KISAN KCC saturation drive.

process: Step 1: Download the simplified one-page KCC application form from pmkisan.gov.in or collect it from your local bank branch.
Step 2: Fill in basic personal details: Name, Aadhaar, PM-KISAN registration number, and residential village.
Step 3: Fill in land details: Survey Number, Village, Title, and crops cultivated (Kharif, Rabi, and Horticulture).
Step 4: Check the declaration certifying you have no existing KCC credit from another branch.
Step 5: Attach copies of Land Record (Khatauni) and Aadhaar card.
Step 6: Submit the application to the branch manager of your local Public Sector Bank, Regional Rural Bank (RRB), or Cooperative Bank.
Step 7: The bank issues an acknowledgement slip; processing must be completed within 14 days under RBI directives.
Step 8: Upon sanction, receive your RuPay KCC Debit Card, which can be swiped at ATMs and fertilizer outlets.

faqs.q: What is the net interest rate on a Kisan Credit Card?
faqs.a: The base rate is 7%. If the farmer repays within 12 months, the Central Government provides a 3% prompt repayment subsidy, making the effective interest rate only 4% per year.

faqs.q: Do I have to pledge land to get a KCC loan?
faqs.a: No collateral/mortgage of land is required for loans up to ₹1,60,000. Loans above ₹1.6 Lakh require hypothecation or land charge.

faqs.q: Can animal husbandry and dairy farmers get a KCC?
faqs.a: Yes. KCC credit limits up to ₹2,00,000 are available specifically for dairy, poultry, sheep, goat, and fisheries farmers without crop land requirements.

faqs.q: Can I use my KCC card at ordinary commercial ATMs?
faqs.a: Yes. The RuPay KCC card functions like any standard bank debit card and can withdraw cash at any ATM in India.

faqs.q: What is the validity period of a Kisan Credit Card?
faqs.a: The credit limit is approved for 5 years, subject to an annual review and rollover of dues.

faqs.q: What happens if I cannot repay due to severe drought?
faqs.a: In cases of notified natural calamities, banks convert short-term KCC loans into medium-term loans repayable over 3 to 5 years, providing immediate moratorium.

purpose: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme provides farmers with timely, flexible, and affordable institutional credit to meet short-term crop cultivation expenses, post-harvest costs, farm maintenance, and allied agricultural needs (dairy, fisheries, animal husbandry) at highly subsidized interest rates.
targetBeneficiary: All individual and joint land-owning cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and self-help groups (SHGs) of farmers, including animal husbandry and fisheries rearers.
financialBenefit: Concessional credit up to ₹3,00,000 at an effective interest rate of only 4% per annum (with collateral-free limit up to ₹1.6 Lakh)
benefitFrequency: Revolving credit limit valid for 5 years
impact: Liberates rural farming households from predatory private moneylenders charging 24–36% interest, provides instant ATM-cum-debit card access to buy seeds and fertilizer, and provides crop insurance linkage.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 18 to 75 years (borrowers above 60 require a legal heir / co-borrower).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Assessed based on scale of finance for crops grown and land holding.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Farmer / cultivator / dairy farmer / fish farmer.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of India with operational farm or livestock in bank's service area.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Individual or joint household borrowers.

mandatoryConditions: Must be engaged in agriculture, dairy, animal husbandry, or inland/marine fisheries
Must hold land ownership documents or registered tenancy/leasing certificate
Must not be an un-rehabilitated willful defaulter at any scheduled bank
conditionalRequirements: Land mortgage / hypothecation required for loan limits exceeding ₹1,60,000.
ineligibility: Willful loan defaulters whose previous agricultural loans have turned NPA without settlement
Persons not engaged in any agricultural, horticultural, or animal husbandry activities
Minors below 18 years
applicationMode: Online via Banking Portals / CSC & Offline at any Commercial, Cooperative, or Gramin Bank
offlineProcess: Walk into your nearest State Bank of India, Gramin Bank, or Cooperative Bank branch where you hold your savings account. Request the Kisan Credit Card application desk. Hand over your Land Khatauni and Aadhaar card. The branch will calculate your crop limit (e.g., ₹50,000 per acre depending on crop) and sanction your RuPay KCC card within 14 working days.
commonMistakes: Applying at multiple banks simultaneously: Centralized credit bureau checks reject duplicate agricultural credit lines.
Delaying annual repayment beyond the due date: To enjoy the 4% net interest rate, farmers must clear dues or rollover the principal once within 12 months.
Assuming KCC is only for crop farmers: Animal husbandry, dairy, and fisheries farmers are also entitled to KCC limits up to ₹2 Lakh at subsidized rates.
processingTime: Maximum 14 working days from receipt of complete application per RBI mandate.
renewalRequired: Credit limit is sanctioned for 5 years with simple annual review.
trackingProcedure: Inquire at the branch manager's desk with your acknowledgement slip or check loan account on mobile banking.
correctionProcedure: Submit updated land records to branch to increase credit limit if additional land is acquired.
disbursementMethod: RuPay KCC Debit Card / Overdraft Drawing Account
disbursementDetails: Farmers are issued a RuPay Kisan Debit Card. Money can be withdrawn anytime from any bank ATM or swiped at PoS machines in fertilizer, seed, and pesticide shops.

name: PM-KUSUM (Solar Pumps for Farmers)
department: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy
applyChannel: your state's implementing agency (links on the PM-KUSUM portal)
description: Subsidised standalone solar pumps and solarisation of grid-connected pumps for farmers.
whoCanApply: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, FPOs and cooperatives, as per state implementation.
benefits: Massive 60% capital subsidy on the cost of solar irrigation pump sets (30% funded by Central Government + 30% by State Government). Farmers contribute only 10% of total cost upfront; the remaining 30% is financed via low-interest bank loan. Excess solar electricity generated can be sold back to state DISCOMs for steady secondary income.
deadlineInfo: Sanctioned in state-wise tranches. State portals open application windows each financial year until district quotas are filled.

rules.label: Has cultivable land for the pump
State agency has an open application window

documents.why: To confirm land title and ownership in farmer's name.

documents.why: Identity verification and DBT subsidy tracking.

process: Step 1: Identify your State Nodal Agency (SNA) portal for PM-KUSUM (e.g. mahadisha.gov.in for Maharashtra, hareda.gov.in for Haryana).
Step 2: Click on 'PM-KUSUM Component B / C Online Application'.
Step 3: Register using your Aadhaar number and Mobile Number.
Step 4: Enter Land details (District, Taluk, Village, Survey Number, Total Acreage).
Step 5: Select requested Solar Pump Capacity (e.g. 3 HP, 5 HP, or 7.5 HP AC/DC Submersible or Surface Pump) based on water depth.
Step 6: Upload Land Record, Aadhaar, Bank Passbook, and photo of water source.
Step 7: Submit the application and receive your Application Reference ID.
Step 8: Field inspection by the state renewable energy agency to verify groundwater depth and site suitability.
Step 9: Upon approval, deposit the 10% farmer share online or via bank challan.
Step 10: Empanelled solar vendor delivers and installs the solar panels, controller, and pump set within 45 to 60 days.

faqs.q: How much money does a farmer actually pay for a 5 HP solar pump?
faqs.a: For a pump costing roughly ₹2,50,000, the central and state governments pay ₹1,50,000 (60%). The farmer pays only around ₹25,000 (10%) upfront; the remaining ₹75,000 can be taken as a concessional bank loan.

faqs.q: Can I sell excess solar power to the government?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Component C (Grid-connected solar pumps), any solar power not used for pumping can be exported into the local electricity grid at feed-in tariffs set by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC).

faqs.q: What capacity solar pump is suitable for my land?
faqs.a: Generally, 3 HP pumps serve up to 5 acres with water table down to 150 ft; 5 HP serves 5–10 acres down to 250 ft; 7.5 HP is used for larger landholdings or deeper borewells.

faqs.q: What happens during cloudy or rainy days?
faqs.a: Modern PM-KUSUM pumps use high-efficiency MPPT controllers that operate at lower RPM even in diffuse light, though output is reduced compared to bright sunny days.

faqs.q: Who handles maintenance if the pump malfunctions?
faqs.a: All empanelled manufacturers must provide 5 years of comprehensive free warranty, repair, and remote maintenance support.

faqs.q: How do I identify fake PM-KUSUM websites?
faqs.a: Always ensure the website domain ends with '.gov.in' or '.nic.in'. Never deposit money into individual private bank accounts or UPI IDs.

purpose: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) enables farmers to install standalone solar water irrigation pumps and solarize existing grid-connected agricultural pumps, slashing high diesel costs and creating a clean, drought-proof renewable energy source while allowing farmers to sell excess green power to the grid.
targetBeneficiary: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, Water User Associations (WUAs), cooperatives, and Panchayats with agricultural land.
financialBenefit: 60% subsidy on solar pump set cost (Farmer pays only 10% cash upfront, 30% bank loan, 60% government subsidy)
benefitFrequency: One-time capital equipment subsidy with 25-year solar operational life
impact: Eliminates diesel bills of ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000 annually per farmer, guarantees daytime reliable water supply for crops, and generates passive income by feeding green power back into the agricultural grid.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Farmer cultivating agricultural land with borewell/water source.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories; special priority quotas for SC/ST and small/marginal farmers.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Indian citizen residing in project area.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: One solar pump installation per operational borewell / farmer household.

mandatoryConditions: Must own agricultural land with an existing functional borewell, open well, or farm pond with adequate water source
For standalone off-grid pumps (Component B), the land must be located in an un-electrified agricultural area or dark zone where grid connection is unavailable or unreliable
Must pay the mandatory 10% farmer share into the nodal agency escrow account upon provisional sanction
conditionalRequirements: No Objection Certificate (NOC) from groundwater authority in notified groundwater over-exploited blocks.
ineligibility: Farmers without any cultivable land or without legal water access rights
Farmers who have already availed capital subsidy for a solar water pump under any other central/state government scheme in the last 10 years
Sites lacking groundwater feasibility
applicationMode: Online through State Renewable Energy Development Agency portal (e.g., MEDA, KREDL, HAREDA, UPNEDA)
offlineProcess: Farmers can visit the District Office of their State Renewable Energy Development Agency (SNA) or the District Agriculture Officer. Staff will guide the farmer through the portal submission and provide payment challans for the 10% beneficiary contribution.
commonMistakes: Falling for fraudulent phishing websites: Only apply on official state government portals ending in .gov.in. MNRE has repeatedly issued notices against fake websites taking advance deposits.
Ordering incorrect pump HP capacity: 3 HP is ideal up to 150-200 feet depth; 5 HP or 7.5 HP is required for deeper borewells exceeding 250 feet.
Site shaded by trees or high structures: Solar arrays require unobstructed direct sunlight from 8 AM to 5 PM.
processingTime: 60 to 90 days from application to physical pump commissioning in field.
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; solar panels come with a 25-year manufacturer performance warranty.
trackingProcedure: Log in to the State Renewable Energy Agency portal using your registration number to track vendor allocation, dispatch, and installation.
correctionProcedure: Request pump capacity modification during the physical field survey before final vendor payment.
disbursementMethod: Direct Capital Subsidy Payment to Empanelled Vendor by MNRE and State Govt
disbursementDetails: The farmer does not handle the 60% subsidy cash. The farmer pays only 10% (plus any loan component); the central and state governments disburse the remaining 60% directly to the empanelled solar equipment manufacturer once installation and remote monitoring geo-tagging are completed.

name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
department: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy
applyChannel: the PM Surya Ghar national portal
description: Subsidy for installing rooftop solar on homes, helping households get free electricity up to a monthly limit.
whoCanApply: Households that own a house with a suitable roof and a valid electricity connection, and have not availed another solar subsidy.
benefits: Direct government capital subsidy deposited into the homeowner's bank account within 30 days of installation: ₹30,000 for a 1 kW solar system; ₹60,000 for a 2 kW solar system; and the maximum subsidy of ₹78,000 for 3 kW and higher systems. Collateral-free, low-interest bank loans (at just 7% interest, ~0.5% above repo rate) available up to ₹2,00,000 through all major banks on the national portal. Generates 300+ units of free power monthly and yields surplus income by selling power to DISCOMs.
deadlineInfo: Universal national mission approved through 2027 to solarize 1 crore Indian households.

rules.label: Owns a house with a roof suitable for solar
Has a valid electricity connection and no previous solar subsidy
