documents.why: To verify consumer connection number, sanctioned electrical load, and DISCOM tariff category.
documents.format: Original or downloaded electronic bill PDF

documents.name: Aadhaar Card of Electricity Consumer
documents.why: Identity verification and DBT subsidy credit.

documents.name: Roof Ownership Proof / House Tax Receipt / Sale Deed
documents.why: Confirms ownership of residential premises and roof rights.
documents.format: Property tax receipt or sale deed copy

documents.name: Cancelled Cheque or Bank Passbook Copy (Aadhaar-Seeded)
documents.why: Direct electronic credit of the ₹30,000–₹78,000 capital subsidy.
documents.format: Clear copy with Account Number, Name, and IFSC

process: Step 1: Download the 'PM-Surya Ghar' mobile app or visit pmsuryaghar.gov.in.
Step 2: Click 'Apply for Rooftop Solar' and register by selecting your State, Power DISCOM, and entering your Electricity Consumer Number.
Step 3: Enter your Mobile Number and Email to complete registration.
Step 4: Log in and enter your roof area, average monthly electricity consumption, and desired solar plant capacity (e.g. 2 kW or 3 kW).
Step 5: Apply for Technical Feasibility Approval (TFR) from your DISCOM through the portal (usually approved online within 15 days).
Step 6: Select any registered solar vendor from the list on the national portal to sign the installation agreement.
Step 7: The vendor installs the solar panels, inverter, and earthing setup on your roof.
Step 8: Submit installation completion details on the portal and apply for Net Meter inspection.
Step 9: DISCOM engineer inspects the installation, connects the bi-directional Net Meter, and generates the Commissioning Certificate on the portal.
Step 10: Submit your bank details and cancelled cheque on the portal; the central subsidy (up to ₹78,000) is credited directly to your bank account within 30 days.

faqs.q: What is the subsidy amount under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana?
faqs.a: The central government provides: ₹30,000 for a 1 kW system; ₹60,000 for a 2 kW system; and the maximum subsidy of ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW or higher capacity.

faqs.q: How much roof area is required for a 3 kW solar plant?
faqs.a: A 3 kW solar rooftop system requires approximately 300 square feet of shadow-free rooftop space and generates roughly 360 to 400 units of clean electricity every month.

faqs.q: Can I get a bank loan to finance the rooftop solar system?
faqs.a: Yes! The national portal is integrated with major public and private banks (SBI, Canara, PNB, BoB, etc.) offering collateral-free loans up to ₹2,00,000 at an attractive interest rate of around 7% per annum (~0.5% above repo rate).

faqs.q: What is Net Metering and how does it reduce my bill to zero?
faqs.a: A Net Meter records both the electricity you draw from the grid and the excess solar power you feed into the grid. Your monthly bill is calculated only on the net difference. If you export more than you consume, you receive electricity credits or cash payments from your DISCOM.

faqs.q: What is the lifespan of a rooftop solar plant?
faqs.a: Tier-1 solar photovoltaic panels have an operational life of 25 years with guaranteed linear power output.

faqs.q: Can residents of housing societies (apartments) apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Individual apartment owners with dedicated roof rights can apply, and Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs) can apply for group housing common area lighting subsidies of ₹18,000 per kW up to 500 kW.

purpose: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2024 with a budget of ₹75,021 crore, is a revolutionary national renewable energy mission that provides massive direct capital subsidies to install residential rooftop solar systems for 1 crore households, providing up to 300 units of free electricity every month and generating passive income through green grid exports.
targetBeneficiary: Individual residential households across India that own an independent house or apartment with a suitable shadow-free roof and an active domestic electricity connection.
financialBenefit: Direct capital subsidy of ₹30,000 (1 kW), ₹60,000 (2 kW), up to ₹78,000 (3 kW+) deposited into bank account + collateral-free bank loans at 7% interest
benefitFrequency: One-time direct capital subsidy + 25 years of free monthly solar electricity and grid revenue
impact: Slashes residential electricity bills to zero, saves Indian families ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 annually, reduces carbon emissions, and creates thousands of green jobs in solar assembly and maintenance.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling (open to all economic strata).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Citizen of India residing in own residential home/apartment.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Must have an active domestic electricity connection in applicant's name.

mandatoryConditions: Must have an active domestic (residential) electricity consumer connection with the local power DISCOM
Must own an unshaded, structurally sound roof capable of supporting solar panel mounting structures
Solar modules and inverters must be procured strictly from registered vendors on the national portal and comply with Domestic Content Requirement (DCR - Made in India cells/modules)
Must install a bi-directional Net Meter approved by the local power DISCOM
conditionalRequirements: Residential Welfare Associations (RWAs) eligible for ₹18,000 per kW subsidy for common area solar lighting up to 500 kW.
ineligibility: Commercial, industrial, or institutional properties (scheme is strictly for residential dwellings)
Imported non-DCR solar panels not certified by MNRE
Properties without legal electricity connection
applicationMode: Online via National Portal for Rooftop Solar (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) / PM Surya Ghar Mobile App
offlineProcess: Homeowners can visit their local Electricity DISCOM divisional office or contact registered solar rooftop vendors listed on pmsuryaghar.gov.in. Vendors handle the paperwork, DISCOM net-metering approvals, and bank loan integration.
commonMistakes: Installing non-DCR (imported) solar panels: MNRE strictly mandates 'Domestic Content Requirement' (DCR) solar cells and modules; imported panels are disqualified from government subsidy.
Mismatch between electricity bill name and bank account: The bank account for subsidy credit must match the name of the electricity consumer.
Installing higher capacity than sanctioned load: If your sanctioned load is 2 kW, apply for load enhancement with your DISCOM before installing a 3 kW solar system.
processingTime: Installation takes 2 to 4 weeks; subsidy credited within 30 days of Net Meter commissioning.
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; solar panels carry a standard 25-year manufacturer performance warranty.
trackingProcedure: Track application, DISCOM feasibility approval, and subsidy disbursement progress on pmsuryaghar.gov.in.
correctionProcedure: Update bank account details on the national portal before final commissioning inspection.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Homeowner's Bank Account from Central Treasury
disbursementDetails: Upon generation of the Net Meter Commissioning Certificate by the DISCOM, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) transfers the subsidy (up to ₹78,000) directly into the homeowner's bank account via PFMS within 30 days.
helpline: PM Surya Ghar National Toll-Free Helpline: 15555

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
department: National Health Mission, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
applyChannel: your ASHA worker, Anganwadi or government health facility
description: Cash assistance to promote institutional deliveries among poor pregnant women.
whoCanApply: Pregnant women — all women in low-performing states and BPL/SC/ST women in other states — delivering in a government or accredited facility.
benefits: Direct cash assistance to mother upon institutional delivery: In Low Performing States (LPS: UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Assam, J&K), mothers receive ₹1,400 (rural) or ₹1,000 (urban). In High Performing States (HPS), BPL/SC/ST mothers receive ₹700 (rural) or ₹600 (urban). In addition, ASHA worker receives incentive for escorting the mother.
deadlineInfo: Payment is processed immediately at delivery or within 30 days of hospital discharge.

documents.name: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) Card
documents.why: Tracks antenatal check-ups (ANC), tetanus injections, and delivery registration.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card of Mother
documents.why: Identity verification and direct DBT transfer.

documents.name: Hospital Delivery & Discharge Slip
documents.why: Proves institutional delivery occurred in an authorized healthcare facility.
documents.format: Signed discharge summary showing date and time of birth

documents.why: For receiving cash assistance via Direct Benefit Transfer.
documents.format: Copy showing account number and IFSC

process: Step 1: Register your pregnancy with the local ASHA or ANM at the nearest Sub-Centre or Anganwadi within the first 12 weeks.
Step 2: Obtain your Mother and Child Protection (MCP) Card and complete at least 3 Antenatal Care (ANC) visits.
Step 3: At the time of labor, call the national ambulance service (108 / 102) or accompany your ASHA to the nearest government hospital/PHC.
Step 4: Complete institutional delivery at the facility.
Step 5: Hand over mother's bank details, Aadhaar card, and MCP card to the hospital maternity clerk.
Step 6: The medical officer verifies the institutional delivery and approves the JSY voucher.
Step 7: The assistance amount is disbursed via PFMS direct bank transfer or account-payee cheque before hospital discharge.

faqs.q: Is the cash benefit given immediately at the hospital?
faqs.a: Yes, in most government hospitals, the cash assistance is transferred to the mother's bank account or handed over via cheque before discharge.

faqs.q: Can JSY benefits be combined with Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)?
faqs.a: Yes! JSY and PMMVY are distinct schemes and mothers can receive BOTH benefits (up to ₹5,000 from PMMVY + ₹1,400 from JSY).

faqs.q: What if a C-section (caesarean) delivery is required?
faqs.a: C-section deliveries in government hospitals are completely free, and JSY provides up to ₹1,500 assistance for hiring private obstetricians in PHCs/CHCs where government specialists are unavailable.

faqs.q: Is ambulance transport to the hospital free?
faqs.a: Yes. Dial 102 or 108 for free Janani Express / National Ambulance transport from home to hospital and return after delivery.

faqs.q: Do mothers in urban areas receive JSY assistance?
faqs.a: Yes, urban mothers receive ₹1,000 in Low Performing States and ₹600 in High Performing States.

faqs.q: Are teenage mothers below 19 years eligible?
faqs.a: Under JSY guidelines, pregnant women must be 19 years of age or older to receive the cash assistance.

purpose: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), under the National Health Mission, is a safe motherhood intervention designed to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional deliveries among poor pregnant women through direct conditional cash assistance.
targetBeneficiary: Pregnant women from BPL, SC, and ST households delivering in public health institutions or accredited private hospitals.
financialBenefit: Direct cash assistance of ₹1,400 (rural) / ₹1,000 (urban) in Low Performing States; ₹700 (rural) / ₹600 (urban) in High Performing States
benefitFrequency: Per institutional childbirth delivery
impact: Encourages women to deliver in healthcare facilities rather than home deliveries, provides critical neonatal care, and lowers maternal mortality ratio (MMR).

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: BPL household status (in Low Performing States, all pregnant women delivering in government health facilities are eligible regardless of age or income).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: All categories in LPS; BPL/SC/ST in HPS.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: In LPS: all deliveries eligible; in HPS: up to two live births.

mandatoryConditions: Must undergo institutional delivery in a government hospital, Primary Health Centre (PHC), Community Health Centre (CHC), or accredited private maternity facility
Must be registered with local ASHA / ANM and possess Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card
Delivery must be documented by birth certificate/discharge slip
conditionalRequirements: BPL certificate or SC/ST caste certificate required in High Performing States.
ineligibility: Home deliveries (except a modest BPL assistance of ₹500 for destitute women)
Deliveries at un-accredited private nursing homes
In HPS, mothers with more than two surviving children who do not belong to SC/ST categories
applicationMode: Offline through Village ASHA / ANM / Sub-Centre / Hospital Maternity Ward
offlineProcess: There is no complex online application. Simply register with your village ASHA worker during pregnancy. When you arrive at the Community Health Centre or District Hospital for delivery, the hospital administration registers the JSY benefit on the spot.
commonMistakes: Not opening a bank account before delivery: Delays cash transfer; pregnant women are advised to open an individual bank account during the 2nd trimester.
Delivering at unaccredited private clinic: Only government facilities and state-accredited private hospitals qualify.
Forgetting MCP card: Always carry the MCP card to the hospital during labor.
processingTime: At discharge or within 7 to 15 days via bank transfer.
renewalRequired: Applicable per delivery event; no renewal.
trackingProcedure: Ask your village ASHA worker or Hospital Medical Superintendent.
correctionProcedure: Correct bank details at the Hospital Superintendent's office if payment bounces.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Mother's Bank Account / Account Payee Cheque
disbursementDetails: Disbursed directly into the mother's bank account via PFMS upon entry into the RCH (Reproductive and Child Health) portal.

name: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (NSAP)
department: Ministry of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme)
applyChannel: your Gram Panchayat / Taluk office or state social security portal
description: Monthly pension for widows from BPL households.
whoCanApply: Widows aged 40–79 belonging to BPL households.
benefits: Monthly pension of ₹300 per month from the Central Government, significantly enhanced by state government contributions (e.g. ₹1,000 to ₹2,500+ per month depending on the state, such as ₹1,500 in Maharashtra, ₹1,000 in UP, ₹1,200 in Karnataka). Beneficiaries who reach 80 years transition automatically to the Indira Gandhi Old Age Pension.
deadlineInfo: Open throughout the year. Applications are verified and sanctioned monthly.

rules.label: Is a widow (husband's death certificate required)

documents.why: Verifies Below Poverty Line economic status.

process: Step 1: Obtain the NSAP Widow Pension application form from your local Gram Panchayat Secretary, BDO office, or Municipal office.
Step 2: Fill in personal details, BPL household ID, date of husband's death, and Aadhaar number.
Step 3: Attach verified copies of: Husband's Death Certificate, BPL Ration Card, Aadhaar Card, and Bank Passbook.
Step 4: Submit to the Gram Panchayat Secretary (rural) or Municipal Ward Officer (urban).
Step 5: Village level social welfare committee / Panchayat verifies BPL status and widowhood.
Step 6: The Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Taluk Social Welfare Officer issues the pension sanction order.
Step 7: Pension is enrolled on the central NSAP-PPS / PFMS system.
Step 8: Monthly pension is credited directly to the widow's bank/post office account on a fixed date every month.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to receive IGNWPS?
faqs.a: Under Central NSAP guidelines, the widow must be at least 40 years of age. (However, many state governments have separate state-funded schemes covering widows below 40 years).

faqs.q: What happens if a widow remarries?
faqs.a: If the beneficiary remarries, she is legally required to inform the Panchayat/BDO and the pension is discontinued.

faqs.q: What happens when the widow turns 80 years old?
faqs.a: Upon attaining 80 years of age, she is automatically migrated to the higher senior citizen tier of the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS).

faqs.q: Can a widow receive this pension if her adult children are earning?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the household is categorized as Below Poverty Line (BPL) in official state records.

faqs.q: How much pension is paid in my state?
faqs.a: While the central share is ₹300, state contributions make the total monthly pension between ₹1,000 and ₹2,500+ depending on your state.

faqs.q: Can the pension be received at home?
faqs.a: Yes, postmen from India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) provide Aadhaar-enabled doorstep cash delivery to elderly widows.

purpose: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) of the Ministry of Rural Development, provides unconditional monthly social pension to destitute widows from BPL households, shielding them from poverty, social vulnerability, and destitution.
targetBeneficiary: Widows aged 40 to 79 years belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.
financialBenefit: Monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹2,500+ (combined central + state contribution transferred via monthly DBT)
benefitFrequency: Monthly direct bank transfer
impact: Provides basic economic dignity, food security, and self-reliance to vulnerable widows without dependent adult support.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Must belong to a household listed in the Below Poverty Line (BPL) database / SECC.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories (General, SC, ST, OBC).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Widow heading or living in a BPL household.

mandatoryConditions: Applicant must be a widow aged between 40 and 79 years
Must produce official Death Certificate of the deceased husband
Family must be classified as Below Poverty Line (BPL) as per central/state guidelines
Must possess an individual Aadhaar-seeded bank or post office savings account
conditionalRequirements: Remarriage disqualifies the widow from continuing the pension.
ineligibility: Widows below 40 years of age (covered under select state-specific widow relief programs)
Widows who have remarried
Non-BPL households
Widows receiving regular government or family pension from deceased husband's government service
applicationMode: Offline at Block Development Office (BDO) / Municipal Ward Office or Online via State Social Welfare / NSAP Portal
offlineProcess: Visit your local Gram Panchayat office or Taluk Tahsildar Social Security counter with your husband's death certificate, BPL card, and Aadhaar card. The staff verifies records and prepares your pension file.
commonMistakes: Applying without official death certificate: A village panchayat certificate may not suffice if a registered death certificate is available; ensure you obtain a computerized death certificate.
Bank account not linked to Aadhaar: Causes monthly pension credits to bounce back to the treasury.
processingTime: 45 to 60 days from application submission to first pension disbursement.
renewalRequired: Annual life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) or non-remarriage declaration submitted once a year.
trackingProcedure: Visit nsap.nic.in, click 'Beneficiary Search' and enter your State, District, and Application Number.
correctionProcedure: Visit the Block Social Welfare Officer to update bank account or address details.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Savings Bank Account / Post Office Account
disbursementDetails: Disbursed monthly via PFMS/DBT directly into the widow's Aadhaar-seeded bank account or post office account on the 1st week of each month.

name: National Family Benefit Scheme (NSAP)
department: Ministry of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme)
description: One-time assistance to a BPL family on the death of its primary breadwinner.
whoCanApply: BPL households whose primary breadwinner (aged 18–59) has died.
benefits: One-time lump-sum cash assistance of ₹20,000 transferred directly into the bank account of the surviving spouse or eligible adult head of the household via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
deadlineInfo: Must apply within 1 year from the date of death of the breadwinner.

documents.name: Death Certificate of Primary Breadwinner
documents.why: Legal proof of date of death and age verification.
documents.issuingAuthority: Registrar of Births and Deaths / Municipal Authority

documents.name: Age Proof of Deceased Breadwinner (Aadhaar / Voter ID / Marksheet)
documents.why: Confirms age was strictly between 18 and 59 years at death.
documents.format: Photocopy showing exact date or year of birth

documents.name: BPL Ration Card / BPL Household Certificate
documents.why: Verifies Below Poverty Line economic status.
documents.issuingAuthority: Food and Civil Supplies Department / BDO

documents.name: Primary Breadwinner & Family Tree Certificate
documents.why: Certifies deceased was the main earner and lists legal surviving heir.
documents.issuingAuthority: Revenue Authority (Tahsildar / Village Patwari / Ward Officer)
documents.format: Signed inquiry report on prescribed proforma

documents.name: Surviving Applicant's Bank Passbook Copy (Aadhaar-Seeded)
documents.why: For receiving ₹20,000 lump sum via DBT.
documents.format: Passbook copy showing Account Number and IFSC

process: Step 1: Obtain the NFBS application form from your local Gram Panchayat Secretary, BDO office, or Municipal Corporation.
Step 2: Fill in details of the deceased breadwinner (Name, Age, Date of Death, Occupation) and surviving applicant details.
Step 3: Attach Death Certificate, Age proof of deceased (18–59 yrs), BPL card, Family Tree report, and Applicant's Bank Passbook.
Step 4: Submit to the Gram Panchayat Secretary (rural) or Municipal Ward Officer (urban).
Step 5: Village Revenue Officer / Patwari conducts inquiry to confirm the deceased was the primary earner.
Step 6: Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / District Social Welfare Officer sanctions the financial grant.
Step 7: The lump-sum amount of ₹20,000 is credited directly into the surviving applicant's bank account via PFMS.
Step 8: Applicant receives SMS notification upon credit.

faqs.q: What is the grant amount under the National Family Benefit Scheme?
faqs.a: A one-time lump-sum cash assistance of ₹20,000 is paid directly to the surviving head of the family.

faqs.q: What is the age criterion for the deceased breadwinner?
faqs.a: The deceased must have died between 18 and 59 years of age (both inclusive).

faqs.q: Can a family receive NFBS if the female earner died?
faqs.a: Yes! The deceased primary breadwinner can be male or female, as long as she was an adult contributor to household income.

faqs.q: Can this grant be combined with widow pension?
faqs.a: Yes! A widow can receive the one-time ₹20,000 NFBS grant AND subsequently apply for the monthly Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension (IGNWPS).

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply after death?
faqs.a: Applications must be filed within 12 months (one year) from the date of death.

faqs.q: Who in the family receives the money?
faqs.a: Priority is given to the surviving spouse (widow/widower); in their absence, it is paid to the eldest surviving child or dependent parent.

purpose: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS), under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) of the Ministry of Rural Development, provides a one-time emergency financial grant to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family upon the premature death of its primary breadwinner, preventing immediate destitution and child labor.
targetBeneficiary: Surviving members of a BPL family upon the death of the primary breadwinner (male or female) aged between 18 and 59 years.
financialBenefit: One-time lump-sum grant of ₹20,000 paid to the surviving household head
benefitFrequency: One-time emergency relief grant
impact: Provides immediate financial cushion to impoverished families following the sudden demise of their primary earner, paying for funeral costs, debts, and children's immediate food security.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Deceased breadwinner must have been between 18 and 59 years of age at the time of death.
detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Deceased primary breadwinner can be male or female.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Must belong to a household listed in the national Below Poverty Line (BPL) database.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Primary economic breadwinner of the family.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (General, SC, ST, OBC).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Surviving spouse, minor children, or dependent parents of the deceased breadwinner.

mandatoryConditions: Deceased person must have been the primary economic earner whose contribution was essential to household survival
Deceased breadwinner must have been between 18 and 59 years of age (both inclusive) at death
Household must be Below Poverty Line (BPL)
Application must be filed within the prescribed time limit (usually within 6 months to 1 year of death)
conditionalRequirements: Post-mortem report or FIR required in case of accidental or unnatural death.
ineligibility: Deaths occurring when the breadwinner was aged 60 years or older
Non-BPL households
Families where the deceased was a government employee covered under state family pension / death gratuity
applicationMode: Offline at Block Development Office (BDO) / Municipal Office or Online via State Social Welfare / NSAP Portal
offlineProcess: Visit your local Block Development Office (BDO) or Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office with the death certificate, BPL card, and revenue inquiry report.
commonMistakes: Deceased age 60 or above: NFBS strictly applies to breadwinners who died between 18 and 59 years; deaths at age 60+ are disqualified.
Delaying application beyond 1 year: Applications must be submitted within the state-notified period (usually within 12 months of death).
processingTime: Disbursed within 30 to 60 days of verification.
renewalRequired: One-time grant; no renewal.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on nsap.nic.in using Application Number.
correctionProcedure: Visit the District Social Welfare Office to rectify bank details.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Surviving Applicant's Bank Account via PFMS
disbursementDetails: Central and state governments disburse the ₹20,000 grant as a single lump-sum credit directly into the surviving spouse's savings account.

name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
department: Ministry of Rural Development
applyChannel: your village's Self-Help Group or Block Mission office
description: Organises rural poor women into Self-Help Groups and supports them with credit, skills and livelihoods.
whoCanApply: Rural poor households, with at least one woman member joining a Self-Help Group.
benefits: Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 per SHG + Community Investment Fund (CIF) up to ₹1,50,000 per SHG + Collateral-free bank loans up to ₹20,00,000 per SHG with an interest subvention subsidy reducing the effective interest rate to 7% per annum (and 4% for prompt repayment in 250 focus districts).
deadlineInfo: Continuous rolling community mission active nationwide.

rules.label: Woman member to join a Self-Help Group

documents.name: SHG Registration & Resolution Book
documents.why: Records group formation, member list, and loan approval resolutions.
documents.issuingAuthority: Gram Panchayat / Block Mission Management Unit (BMMU)
documents.format: Original physical register / LokOS digital entry

documents.name: Aadhaar Card of All SHG Members
documents.why: Identity verification and bank account KYC.

documents.name: SHG Bank Passbook (Joint Account)
documents.why: For revolving funds, CIF, and loan disbursements.

process: Step 1: Join or form a Self-Help Group (SHG) of 10–20 neighborhood women facilitated by the Community Resource Person (CRP).
Step 2: Elect Group President, Secretary, and Treasurer; open a joint bank account in the SHG's name.
Step 3: Practice 'Panchasutra' (weekly meetings, weekly savings of ₹50–₹100 per member, internal micro-lending, and record keeping).
Step 4: After 3 months of regular functioning, the SHG receives a Revolving Fund (₹20,000–₹30,000) from the Block Mission Unit.
Step 5: Prepare a Micro-Credit Plan (MCP) outlining members' livelihood credit needs (e.g. buying cows, sewing machines, setting up grocery shops).
Step 6: Bank evaluates SHG grading and sanctions First Tranche Bank Loan (up to ₹1,00,000 to ₹1,50,000).
Step 7: Repay regular monthly bank installments; progress to Second Tranche (₹3,00,000 to ₹5,00,000) and Third Tranche (up to ₹10,00,000–₹20,00,000).
Step 8: Receive central interest subvention directly into the SHG loan account, reducing interest to 7% (or 4%).

faqs.q: What is the maximum collateral-free loan an SHG can receive?
faqs.a: Under RBI guidelines, Women Self-Help Groups under DAY-NRLM can receive collateral-free bank loans up to ₹20,00,000 (Twenty Lakh Rupees).

faqs.q: What are the 'Panchasutra' principles?
faqs.a: The 5 golden rules: 1) Regular weekly meetings, 2) Regular savings, 3) Regular internal lending, 4) Timely loan repayment, and 5) Transparent bookkeeping.

faqs.q: What is the net interest rate paid by SHGs?
faqs.a: All women SHGs receive interest subvention from the central government reducing the interest rate to 7% per annum. In 250 focus districts, prompt repayment reduces it further to just 4%.

faqs.q: What is a Lakhpati Didi under DAY-NRLM?
faqs.a: Lakhpati Didi is a flagship government mission to train and support SHG women to earn a sustainable annual household income of ₹1,00,000 or more through diversified livelihoods.

faqs.q: Can an individual woman get a loan without joining an SHG?
faqs.a: NRLM operates strictly through community groups. An individual woman must be part of an SHG to access revolving funds and group credit lines.

faqs.q: Who provides training on starting small businesses?
faqs.a: State Rural Livelihood Missions provide free training in dairy farming, tailoring, food processing, poultry, organic farming, and digital payments through Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis.

purpose: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, organizes poor rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and provides continuous financial, technical, and credit support to establish diversified micro-enterprises and achieve sustainable household livelihoods.
targetBeneficiary: Rural women belonging to poor households, with at least one woman member from every identified poor rural household mobilized into a Self Help Group (SHG).
financialBenefit: Revolving Fund (₹20,000–₹30,000) + CIF (up to ₹1.5 Lakh) + Collateral-free bank linkage loans up to ₹20 Lakh at 7% interest
benefitFrequency: Phased capital infusion, revolving credit, and subsidized bank enterprise loans
impact: Has mobilized over 10 crore rural women into 90 lakh SHGs across India, building financial resilience, rural micro-enterprises, dairy cooperatives, and women-led rural agribusinesses.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Identified through Participatory Identification of the Poor (PIP) process / SECC 2011.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Rural agricultural workers, artisans, weavers, dairy workers, and homemakers.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Special focus on SC, ST, primitive tribal groups, and minority households.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: One woman per poor rural household.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an active member of an affinity-based Self-Help Group (10 to 20 women members) practicing the 'Panchasutra' (Regular Meetings, Regular Savings, Regular Internal Lending, Regular Recovery, and Up-to-date Bookkeeping)
SHG must open a joint savings bank account and be graded by the bank for credit linkage
Must be identified as poor through the Village Organization (VO) Participatory Identification process
conditionalRequirements: Prompt repayment of bank loans required to receive the 3% interest subvention rebate.
ineligibility: Individuals not part of a registered SHG
Urban residents (covered under separate DAY-NULM urban scheme)
SHGs that do not practice regular weekly savings or bookkeeping
applicationMode: Through Village Organization (VO) / Cluster Level Federation (CLF) / Block Mission Management Unit (BMMU)
offlineProcess: Meet the Community Resource Person (CRP), Village Organization (VO) office-bearers, or the Block Programme Manager (BPM) at your local Block Development Office (BDO).
commonMistakes: Irregular meetings and bookkeeping: Banks grade SHGs based on regular attendance and ledger maintenance; poor records halt loan sanctions.
Defaulting on internal loans: Members must return borrowings to the group corpus to maintain high creditworthiness.
processingTime: Revolving fund released within 3 months of formation; bank credit within 6 months.
renewalRequired: Continuous revolving credit with graduated credit limit increases upon loan clearance.
trackingProcedure: Track SHG profile and loan status on the national LokOS mobile app and nrlm.gov.in.
correctionProcedure: Village Organization and Community Resource Persons resolve ledger discrepancies.
disbursementMethod: Direct Electronic Fund Transfer to SHG Joint Bank Account
disbursementDetails: Funds (RF, CIF, and Bank Loans) are credited directly into the SHG's bank account. The group then disburses loans to individual members based on the approved Micro-Credit Plan.

name: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)
department: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
applyChannel: a post office or authorised bank branch
description: Government-backed savings scheme giving senior citizens a regular quarterly interest income.
whoCanApply: Individuals aged 60+ (and certain retirees aged 55–60 under conditions).
benefits: Guaranteed high interest rate of 8.2% per annum, paid out every quarter directly into the senior citizen's savings account. Investment ceiling up to ₹30,00,000 (Thirty Lakh Rupees, enhanced in 2023 from ₹15 Lakh). Qualifies for Section 80C income tax deduction up to ₹1,50,000 per year.
deadlineInfo: VRS retirees (55–59) must open account within 3 months of retirement; open year-round for citizens 60+.

rules.label: Has a bank / post office account

documents.name: PAN Card
documents.why: Mandatory for tax compliance and interest payout TDS tracking.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Identity and address proof.

documents.name: Age / Retirement Proof (for VRS retirees aged 55–59)
documents.why: Proves superannuation / voluntary retirement date within last 3 months.

documents.name: Recent Passport Size Photographs
documents.why: Account opening KYC.

process: Step 1: Visit any Post Office branch or authorized commercial bank (SBI, PNB, BoB, Canara, ICICI, HDFC, etc.).
Step 2: Collect Form-A (Application for Opening of SCSS Account).
Step 3: Fill in senior citizen's details, deposit amount (up to ₹30 Lakh), and choose individual or joint holding with spouse.
Step 4: Attach PAN Card copy, Aadhaar copy, 2 photos, and retirement proof (if applicable).
Step 5: Deposit funds via cheque or demand draft (cash allowed up to ₹1,00,000).
Step 6: The bank/post office issues the SCSS Passbook or Certificate of Deposit.
Step 7: Interest at 8.2% is calculated and deposited automatically every quarter directly into your linked savings account.
Step 8: Maturity occurs after 5 years, with the option to extend for an additional 3-year block.

faqs.q: What is the maximum investment limit in SCSS?
faqs.a: In Budget 2023, the maximum investment ceiling was doubled to ₹30,00,000 (Thirty Lakh Rupees) per individual. A husband and wife aged 60+ can invest up to ₹60 Lakh combined in separate accounts.

faqs.q: What is the current interest rate?
faqs.a: The scheme offers an attractive 8.2% annual interest rate, fully backed by sovereign government guarantee.

faqs.q: When is the interest paid?
faqs.a: Interest is paid quarterly on the 1st of April, 1st of July, 1st of October, and 1st of January directly into your linked savings bank account.

faqs.q: Can I extend the account after 5 years?
faqs.a: Yes. After the initial 5-year maturity, you can extend the account for an additional block of 3 years by submitting an extension application within 1 year of maturity.

faqs.q: Can premature withdrawal be made?
faqs.a: Yes. Premature closure is permitted after 1 year with a nominal 1.5% deduction, and after 2 years with a 1% deduction on the principal amount.

faqs.q: Is the investment eligible for Section 80C tax deduction?
faqs.a: Yes. Investments in SCSS qualify for income tax deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1,50,000 per financial year.

purpose: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS), administered by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, provides a safe, sovereign-backed, high-yield quarterly income stream for senior citizens, ensuring secure retirement cash flow and financial stability.
targetBeneficiary: Senior citizens aged 60 years and above (or 55+ for voluntary retirees/VRS and 50+ for retired defense personnel).
financialBenefit: High 8.2% guaranteed annual interest paid quarterly + Tax deduction up to ₹1.5 Lakh under Section 80C
benefitFrequency: Quarterly interest payment credited automatically on the 1st of April, July, October, and January
impact: Provides reliable regular quarterly income to pensioners, insulates elderly citizens from stock market volatility, and protects retirement gratuity and savings with 100% sovereign safety.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 60 years and above (55+ for civilian VRS/superannuation; 50+ for retired defense personnel).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO income limit (open to all senior citizens).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Retired senior citizens / any senior citizen.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident Indian senior citizens (NRIs and HUFs not eligible).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Can be held individually or jointly with spouse.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an Indian citizen aged 60 years or older (or 55+ for VRS retirees applying within 3 months of retirement)
Deposit must be in multiples of ₹1,000, up to a maximum cumulative limit of ₹30,00,000 across all SCSS accounts
Must hold a valid PAN card and Aadhaar card
conditionalRequirements: Retirement benefit disbursement certificate required for applicants aged 55 to 59 years applying under VRS.
ineligibility: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs)
Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs)
Citizens below 60 years who did not retire under voluntary retirement schemes
applicationMode: Offline at any Post Office or authorized Public/Private Sector Bank branch
offlineProcess: Walk into your local Post Office or commercial bank branch with your PAN card, Aadhaar card, and cheque for the deposit amount. The branch manager will open your account and issue your passbook.
commonMistakes: Exceeding ₹30 Lakh limit across accounts: The ₹30 Lakh ceiling is cumulative per individual across all banks and post offices combined.
Not submitting Form 15H: Interest exceeding ₹50,000/year attracts TDS; submit Form 15H annually if your total income is below the taxable threshold.
processingTime: Account opened within 24 to 48 hours.
renewalRequired: Account matures after 5 years; can be extended for an additional 3 years by submitting Form-4.
trackingProcedure: Track quarterly interest credits in your linked savings bank account or update your SCSS passbook.
correctionProcedure: Submit nomination update form or account transfer request at your bank branch.
disbursementMethod: Direct Electronic Quarterly Interest Transfer to Linked Savings Bank Account
disbursementDetails: Quarterly interest is credited automatically on the first day of April, July, October, and January directly into the senior citizen's savings account.
helpline: National Savings Institute / Post Office Helpline: 1800-266-6868

department: Social Welfare & Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu

description: Monthly assistance for girls who studied Class 6–12 in Tamil Nadu government schools and join higher education.
whoCanApply: Girl students who studied Class 6 to 12 in TN government schools and are pursuing higher education (degree, diploma, ITI).
benefits: Direct financial assistance of ₹1,000 per month credited directly into the girl student's bank account every month until the successful completion of her degree or diploma course.
deadlineInfo: College enrollment window: opens in July/August every academic year.

process: Step 1: Enrol in any recognized degree, diploma, or ITI course in Tamil Nadu.
Step 2: Collect your EMIS (Education Management Information System) number from your school or college.
Step 3: College scholarship nodal officer opens your profile on pudhumaipenn.tn.gov.in.
Step 4: System enters EMIS number, which auto-verifies that you studied in government schools from Class 6 to 12.
Step 5: Student provides Aadhaar card and Bank Account details.
Step 6: College Principal verifies and forwards application electronically to the Social Welfare Department.
Step 7: District Social Welfare Officer approves the sanction order.
Step 8: ₹1,000 is credited directly into the student's bank account every month via DBT.

faqs.q: Is there any family income ceiling for Pudhumai Penn?
faqs.a: No! There is no family income ceiling. Any girl who studied from Class 6 to Class 12 in a Tamil Nadu Government school is eligible regardless of family income.

faqs.q: Can engineering and medical students get this benefit?
faqs.a: Yes! B.E., B.Tech, MBBS, BDS, Law, Agriculture, Arts, Science, Diploma, and ITI students are all eligible.

faqs.q: Can I receive this scholarship in addition to other community scholarships?
faqs.a: Yes. Pudhumai Penn is an incentive scheme and can be availed in addition to standard SC/ST/BC/MBC post-matric scholarships.

faqs.q: What if I studied Class 6 to 10 in a government school but Class 11 and 12 in a private school?
faqs.a: You must have studied continuously from Class 6 through Class 12 in government schools; partial private school education disqualifies the candidate.

faqs.q: Is the money stopped during summer vacation?
faqs.a: The benefit of ₹1,000 per month is paid consistently throughout the academic calendar year.

faqs.q: What is the equivalent scheme for boy students?
faqs.a: The Tamil Nadu Government launched the 'Tamizh Pudhalvan' scheme providing ₹1,000/month for boys who studied in government schools.

purpose: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme (Pudhumai Penn), launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu, provides monthly financial assistance to girl students who studied in government schools from Class 6 to 12, incentivizing female higher education and curbing child marriage.
targetBeneficiary: Girl students who studied in Tamil Nadu Government schools from Class 6 to Class 12 and are enrolled in recognized undergraduate degree, diploma, ITI, or professional courses.
financialBenefit: ₹1,00,000 per month (₹12,000 per year) directly credited until completion of degree/diploma
benefitFrequency: Monthly direct bank transfer
impact: Boosted female college admissions by over 27% across Tamil Nadu, empowered young women to complete higher education independently, and prevented early marriages.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling (open to all girls who studied in government schools).
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Must have studied continuously from Class 6 to Class 12 in Tamil Nadu Government schools.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Student enrolled in undergraduate degree, diploma, or ITI course in Tamil Nadu.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Covered per eligible female student.

Must be currently enrolled in an approved undergraduate degree, diploma, engineering, medical, or ITI course
Must possess an active individual bank account seeded with Aadhaar
conditionalRequirements: Transfer Certificate (TC) or EMIS school verification confirming government schooling from Class 6 to 12.
ineligibility: Students who studied in private schools (even if under RTE) or private aided schools for any period between Class 6 and 12
Male students
Students pursuing postgraduate courses (scheme covers undergraduate/diploma only)

offlineProcess: Students do not need to visit government offices. The application is facilitated directly inside your college by the designated College Pudhumai Penn Nodal Officer during admission.
commonMistakes: Studying in government-aided school: Only students of 100% government schools qualify (aided schools are covered under a separate scheme).
Bank account in parents' name: Account must strictly be in the girl student's own individual name.
processingTime: First payment credited within 30 to 45 days of college verification.
renewalRequired: Auto-renewed each semester upon college confirmation of student's continued attendance.
trackingProcedure: Check status on pudhumaipenn.tn.gov.in using Aadhaar number or mobile number.
correctionProcedure: Contact your college nodal officer to correct bank details or EMIS records.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Student's Bank Account
disbursementDetails: Tamil Nadu Social Welfare Department deposits ₹1,000 on the 1st week of every month directly into the girl student's bank account.

benefits: Direct unconditional financial transfer of ₹1,000 per month credited directly into the woman's Aadhaar-seeded bank account on the 15th of every month.

process: Step 1: Receive application token and form distributed at your doorstep by your local Fair Price Shop ration dealer.
Step 2: Attend the designated KMUT Registration Camp on your specified token date and time.
Step 3: Submit the filled application along with your Smart Ration Card, Aadhaar, and EB Consumer Number.
Step 4: The camp volunteer enters your details into the official KMUT mobile app.
Step 5: Perform biometric fingerprint authentication.
Step 6: An automated SMS confirmation with Application ID is sent to your mobile phone.
Step 7: Revenue authorities perform automated cross-verification with TANGEDCO, Land Records, and Income Tax databases.
Step 8: Once approved, ₹1,000 is credited directly into your bank account on the 15th of every month.
Step 9: If rejected, appeal online via e-Sevai or at the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) office within 30 days.

faqs.q: On what day of the month is the KMUT money deposited?
faqs.a: The ₹1,000 assistance is deposited directly into the beneficiary's bank account on the 15th of every calendar month.

faqs.q: What should I do if my application was rejected?
faqs.a: You can file an appeal online through any e-Sevai centre or submit a petition to the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) within 30 days of receiving the rejection SMS.

faqs.q: Can an unmarried or divorced woman living alone apply?
faqs.a: Yes, single women, widows, and female heads of families holding a separate Smart Ration Card are fully eligible.

faqs.q: What is the electricity unit limit?
faqs.a: The total domestic electricity consumption of the household must be less than 3,600 units per year (an average of 300 units per month).

faqs.q: Can government pensioners apply?
faqs.a: No. Households with regular government employees or pensioners are excluded from the scheme.

faqs.q: Is there any charge for registration or appeals?
faqs.a: No. The application and appeal process are completely free of charge.

purpose: Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai (KMUT) Scheme, launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu, provides monthly rights-based financial support of ₹1,000 to women heads of eligible households in Tamil Nadu, recognizing women's invisible unpaid domestic labor and improving their economic independence.
targetBeneficiary: Eligible women heads of families in Tamil Nadu aged 21 years and older meeting basic economic livelihood criteria.
financialBenefit: ₹1,000 per month (₹12,000 per year) directly credited via monthly DBT
benefitFrequency: Monthly direct bank transfer
impact: Empowered over 1.15 crore women in Tamil Nadu to manage household emergencies, support children's nutritional needs, and build personal savings.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Must have completed 21 years of age.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Annual family income must be less than ₹2,50,000 per annum.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Informal laborers, agricultural workers, domestic helpers, self-employed women, and homemakers.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories residing in Tamil Nadu.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of Tamil Nadu with active Smart Ration Card.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Family land holding must be below 5 acres wetland or 10 acres dry land; domestic electricity consumption must be below 3,600 units per year.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an adult woman aged 21 years or older
Family annual income must not exceed ₹2,50,000
Family must not own four-wheeler (except commercial taxi, auto, or agricultural tractor)
Domestic household electricity consumption must be below 3,600 units annually
Must possess active Smart Family Ration Card in Tamil Nadu
conditionalRequirements: In families where a male is listed as head on the Smart Card, the wife is treated as the woman head of household.
ineligibility: Families with annual income exceeding ₹2,50,000
Families where any member pays income tax or professional tax
Central or State Government employees, public sector employees, bank employees, and pensioners
Elected representatives (MPs, MLAs, Panchayat Presidents, Municipal Councillors)
Families owning four-wheelers for personal use
applicationMode: Special Application Camps at Fair Price Shops & e-Sevai Centres across Tamil Nadu
offlineProcess: Registration is conducted through decentralized neighborhood camps organized at local schools, ration shops, and community halls across every ward and village in Tamil Nadu.
commonMistakes: Domestic electricity bill exceeding 3,600 units/year: Check your annual TANGEDCO consumption before applying.
Family member filing income tax: Auto-detected via PAN-Aadhaar linkage and disqualified.
Unlinked bank account: Must ensure your bank account is seeded with Aadhaar on NPCI.
openingDate: Rolling appeals and enrollments open year-round
processingTime: Appeals processed within 30 days by Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).
renewalRequired: No renewal needed; payments continue uninterrupted on the 15th of every month.
trackingProcedure: Visit kmut.tn.gov.in or inquire at your local e-Sevai centre with your Smart Card number.
correctionProcedure: File an appeal petition at your nearest e-Sevai Centre or RDO office.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Woman's Bank Account via Tamil Nadu State Treasury
disbursementDetails: The Government of Tamil Nadu deposits ₹1,000 directly into the woman beneficiary's bank account on the 15th of every calendar month.
helpline: KMUT Tamil Nadu Helpline: 044-25619208 or CM Helpline 1100

name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (Tamil Nadu)
department: Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
description: Cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals for low-income Tamil Nadu families, integrated with PM-JAY.
whoCanApply: Tamil Nadu families with annual income up to ₹1.2 lakh (and certain notified categories).
benefits: Comprehensive cashless coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year for 1,513 medical and surgical procedures across 1,000+ empanelled public and private hospitals in Tamil Nadu, including diagnostic charges, ICU, diagnostic tests, and follow-up care. Covers organ transplants, cancer treatment, and heart surgeries.
deadlineInfo: Year-round rolling enrolment. No deadline.

process: Step 1: Obtain an Income Certificate showing annual family income under ₹1,20,000 from your local e-Sevai Centre / Tahsildar.
Step 2: Take your original Smart Family Card, Income Certificate, and family Aadhaar cards to the CMCHIS Enrolment Kiosk at the District Collectorate.
Step 3: CMCHIS field verification officer verifies your documents.
Step 4: Biometric fingerprint and live photograph of all family members are captured.
Step 5: The Smart CMCHIS URN (Unique Registration Number) card is printed and handed over on the spot.
Step 6: Present this card at any empanelled hospital in Tamil Nadu for cashless admission.

faqs.q: Is CMCHIS linked with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.a: Yes. Tamil Nadu co-brands CMCHIS with PM-JAY. Eligible families receive seamless cashless benefits up to ₹5,00,000 under the integrated platform.

faqs.q: What is the income ceiling to qualify for CMCHIS?
faqs.a: The family's total annual income from all sources must be less than ₹1,20,000 per year.

faqs.q: Does the scheme cover high-cost organ transplants?
faqs.a: Yes. CMCHIS provides dedicated packages for renal (kidney) transplant, liver transplant, bone marrow transplant, and heart valve replacement.

faqs.q: Where can I get the CMCHIS Smart Card made?
faqs.a: At the dedicated CMCHIS counter inside every District Collector's Office in Tamil Nadu.

faqs.q: Can emergency accident victims be treated immediately without the card?
faqs.a: Yes. In life-threatening emergency situations, empanelled hospitals admit patients immediately and obtain emergency pre-authorization within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Are diagnostic scans like MRI and CT covered?
faqs.a: Yes, pre-operative and diagnostic evaluations related to surgical inpatient packages are covered.

purpose: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS) was launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu to provide cashless multi-speciality medical and surgical hospitalisation cover to low-income families in Tamil Nadu, eliminating financial distress from high-cost tertiary medical treatments.
targetBeneficiary: Families in Tamil Nadu whose annual household income is less than ₹1,20,000, as verified through Tamil Nadu Smart Ration Card.
financialBenefit: Up to ₹5,00,000 cashless cover per family per year across 1,513 notified medical procedures
benefitFrequency: Annual floating family coverage
impact: Provides gold-standard surgical and tertiary healthcare access in Tamil Nadu's top hospitals to working-class, agrarian, and informal sector households.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: All family members listed on the Tamil Nadu Smart Ration Card.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Family annual income strictly below ₹1,20,000 per annum.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Informal, agricultural, and unorganized workers, daily wage laborers.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories residing in Tamil Nadu.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of Tamil Nadu with active Smart Ration Card.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Family is defined as head of family, spouse, dependent children, and dependent parents as per Smart Card.

mandatoryConditions: Must hold a valid Tamil Nadu Smart Family Card (Ration Card)
Annual family income must not exceed ₹1,20,000 as certified by Village Administrative Officer (VAO) / Revenue Authority
Treatment must be availed at an empanelled CMCHIS hospital in Tamil Nadu
conditionalRequirements: Referral or pre-authorisation required for elective multi-speciality surgeries.
ineligibility: Families whose annual income exceeds ₹1,20,000
Tamil Nadu State and Central Government employees and pensioners (covered under separate Government Employee New Health Insurance Scheme)
Persons not residing in Tamil Nadu or without Tamil Nadu Smart Ration Card
applicationMode: Offline at District Collectorate CMCHIS Kiosk / e-Sevai Centres
offlineProcess: Visit the CMCHIS special counter located inside the District Collector's Office in your district headquarters. The service is free of cost and issues biometric health cards.
commonMistakes: Income certificate older than one year: Must renew income certificate via e-Sevai before card renewal.
Family member not listed on Smart Ration card: Must first add newly married spouses or infants to the PDS Smart card before they can receive hospitalisation cover.
processingTime: Same-day card issuance at District Collectorate; hospital pre-authorisation within 12 hours.
renewalRequired: Card validity runs continuously as long as the Smart Ration card remains active.
trackingProcedure: Search your URN or Ration Card number on cmchistn.com to view policy and claims.
correctionProcedure: Visit the District Collectorate CMCHIS desk to update family member additions.
disbursementMethod: 100% Cashless Inpatient Hospitalisation Settlement
disbursementDetails: Hospital submits online pre-authorization to the Third Party Administrator (TPA) / United India Insurance. Claims are settled directly with the hospital with zero out-of-pocket payment from the patient.

name: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (Maharashtra)
department: Public Health Department, Government of Maharashtra
description: Cashless health insurance for Maharashtra families, integrated with PM-JAY.
whoCanApply: Maharashtra families holding a valid ration card or domicile proof as per current scheme expansion.
benefits: Cashless hospitalisation coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year (raised from ₹1.5 Lakh) across 1,356 medical and surgical therapies in 1,000+ empanelled government and private network hospitals across Maharashtra.
deadlineInfo: Universal year-round coverage. Active 365 days a year.

documents.name: Maharashtra Ration Card (Yellow / Orange / White)
documents.why: Establishes family membership and eligibility under Maharashtra health mission.
documents.issuingAuthority: Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Dept, Maharashtra

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Identity and biometric authentication at hospital Arogyamitra desk.

process: Step 1: Check the list of empanelled network hospitals on jeevandayee.gov.in.
Step 2: Visit the network hospital and approach the 'Arogyamitra' helpdesk near the casualty/admission counter.
Step 3: Show your Maharashtra Ration Card and Aadhaar card to the Arogyamitra.
Step 4: The Arogyamitra searches your family on the MJPJAY web portal and verifies details.
Step 5: Hospital doctor examines the patient and issues an electronic pre-authorization request.
Step 6: State Health Assurance Society (SHAS) medical specialists review and approve the request online (usually within 12 hours).
Step 7: The patient receives complete cashless surgery, medications, diagnostic tests, and food during hospital stay.
Step 8: At discharge, the patient receives 10 days of post-operative medicines and a free follow-up consultation voucher without paying any money.

faqs.q: Is MJPJAY now available to White Ration Card holders too?
faqs.a: Yes! In July 2023, the Maharashtra Government expanded MJPJAY to ALL citizens of Maharashtra, including White Ration cardholders, with coverage increased to ₹5 Lakh.

faqs.q: Do I need a special card or does my Ration Card suffice?
faqs.a: Your existing Maharashtra Ration Card (Yellow, Orange, or White) along with your Aadhaar card is sufficient to avail treatment at any empanelled hospital.

faqs.q: What should I do if an empanelled hospital asks for a deposit?
faqs.a: Do NOT pay. Call the 24/7 State Health Helpline immediately on 155388 or 1800-233-2200 and report the hospital name.

faqs.q: Are cancer surgeries and chemotherapy covered?
faqs.a: Yes. MJPJAY has extensive coverage for medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.

faqs.q: Can kidney dialysis be availed cashlessly?
faqs.a: Yes. Dialysis sessions for patients with end-stage renal disease are fully covered across empanelled dialysis centers.

faqs.q: Does the scheme cover ICU bed charges?
faqs.a: Yes, intensive care unit (ICU) charges, nursing, and medicines during hospitalisation are fully inclusive in the package.

purpose: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY) is the flagship universal health insurance initiative of the Government of Maharashtra. In 2023, the scheme was expanded to cover ALL 12.5 crore citizens of Maharashtra, ensuring cashless secondary and tertiary medical care across state hospitals.
targetBeneficiary: All families residing in Maharashtra holding an active Ration Card and Aadhaar card (Universal coverage across Maharashtra).
financialBenefit: Up to ₹5,00,000 cashless hospitalisation cover per family per year
benefitFrequency: Annual floating family coverage
impact: Protects millions of families from catastrophic medical impoverishment, covers major surgical interventions, pediatric surgeries, cancer care, and cardiac care completely cashlessly.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Universal across Maharashtra (Yellow, Orange, and White ration card holders).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Any occupation (open to all citizens of Maharashtra).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: All categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Covered on family floater basis as per Ration Card.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a resident of Maharashtra holding a valid Ration Card (Yellow, Saffron/Orange, or White Card) or Domicile Certificate
Must possess an individual Aadhaar Card
Treatment must be availed at an empanelled public or private MJPJAY network hospital
conditionalRequirements: Referral from government hospital or Arogyamitra required for elective specialised tertiary procedures.
ineligibility: Non-residents of Maharashtra without state ration card/domicile
Treatments not listed in the 1,356 notified therapy packages
Un-empanelled private hospitals
applicationMode: Direct Cashless Walk-in at any Network Hospital Arogyamitra Desk
offlineProcess: Walk into any empanelled hospital in Maharashtra with your Ration Card and Aadhaar card. The hospital Arogyamitra facilitates the entire pre-authorisation and admission process.
commonMistakes: Paying cash to the hospital upfront: MJPJAY is 100% cashless. If an empanelled hospital demands money, immediately contact the Arogyamitra or call 155388.
Visiting non-empanelled clinics: Only designated network hospitals can provide cashless MJPJAY treatments.
processingTime: Pre-authorisation approved within 6 to 12 hours; emergency cases approved within 2 hours.
renewalRequired: Auto-renews every year on 1st April.
trackingProcedure: Call 155388 or check status on jeevandayee.gov.in.
correctionProcedure: Update name/members on your Ration card at the Tahsildar / Rationing Office.
disbursementMethod: 100% Cashless Treatment Settlement between Government and Hospital
disbursementDetails: No cash is paid to the patient. The State Health Assurance Society pays the hospital directly through online banking based on pre-set package rates.

name: Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana (Maharashtra)
department: Women & Child Development Department, Government of Maharashtra
applyChannel: the Ladki Bahin portal / Anganwadi / Setu centres
description: Monthly financial assistance for women in Maharashtra.
whoCanApply: Women aged 21–65 residing in Maharashtra (married, widowed, divorced, abandoned or one unmarried woman per family) with family income up to ₹2.5 lakh.
benefits: Direct financial assistance of ₹1,500 per month transferred directly into the woman's Aadhaar-seeded bank account every month via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
deadlineInfo: Rolling enrollment open year-round across Maharashtra.

process: Step 1: Download the 'Nari Shakti Doot' mobile app from Google Play Store or visit ladkibahin.maharashtra.gov.in.
Step 2: Register using your Mobile Number and verify via OTP.
Step 3: Select 'Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana'.
Step 4: Enter Applicant's Name as per Aadhaar, Date of Birth, Address, and Marital Status.
Step 5: Enter Maharashtra Ration Card number and upload a clear photo of the Ration Card.
Step 6: Upload photo of Aadhaar Card, Domicile Proof, and Bank Passbook.
Step 7: Provide Aadhaar-seeded bank account details (Bank Name, Account Number, IFSC).
Step 8: Submit the application and download the Acknowledgement PDF.
Step 9: Local Anganwadi Worker / Ward Committee verifies application online.
Step 10: Approved beneficiaries receive ₹1,500 credited directly into their bank account every month.

faqs.q: Is an Income Certificate mandatory for all applicants?
faqs.a: No! If you hold a Yellow or Orange (Saffron) Ration Card, you do NOT need an income certificate; your ration card is accepted as sufficient income proof.

faqs.q: Can unmarried women apply for Ladki Bahin?
faqs.a: Yes. Unmarried adult women between 21 and 65 years who meet the family income criteria are eligible.

faqs.q: Can two women from the same family apply?
faqs.a: Only one eligible woman per ration card can receive the benefit.

faqs.q: What should I do if my money hasn't arrived?
faqs.a: Visit your bank branch and check if your account is seeded with Aadhaar on the NPCI mapper, or check status on the Nari Shakti Doot app.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for this scheme?
faqs.a: The woman must be between 21 and 65 years of age.

faqs.q: Can women receiving other pensions apply?
faqs.a: If a woman is already receiving ₹1,500 or more per month from Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Yojana or another government pension, she cannot receive duplicate benefits.

purpose: Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana, launched by the Government of Maharashtra in July 2024, provides unconditional monthly financial assistance of ₹1,500 to women in Maharashtra, promoting economic empowerment, nutritional security, and decision-making authority in their families.
targetBeneficiary: Women residents of Maharashtra aged 21 to 65 years whose total family annual income does not exceed ₹2,50,000 per annum.
financialBenefit: ₹1,500 per month (₹18,000 per year) directly credited via monthly DBT
benefitFrequency: Monthly direct bank transfer
impact: Benefits over 1.8 crore women across Maharashtra, enabling women to cover health expenses, nutritional needs, children's school fees, and micro-savings.

detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Strictly Female applicant (married, widowed, divorced, abandoned, or unmarried adult women).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Total family annual income must NOT exceed ₹2,50,000 per annum (Orange and Yellow ration card holders exempt from separate income certificate).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Informal workers, agricultural laborers, self-employed women, and homemakers.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Domicile / permanent resident of Maharashtra (15+ years).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Only one eligible woman per household holding Yellow/Orange Ration Card.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an adult woman aged 21 to 65 years
Must be a resident of Maharashtra holding a Maharashtra Domicile Certificate, 15-year Ration Card, Voter ID, or School Leaving Certificate
Total family annual income must not exceed ₹2,50,000 per year
Must possess an active individual bank account seeded with Aadhaar for NPCI DBT
Neither applicant nor any family member should be paying income tax or regular government employees
conditionalRequirements: Yellow and Orange (Saffron) ration card holders do NOT require a separate income certificate.
ineligibility: Women from families whose annual income exceeds ₹2,50,000
Families where any member pays income tax
Families where any member is a regular/contractual government employee, semi-government employee, or pensioner
Families owning a four-wheeler (except commercial agricultural tractor)
Women already receiving ₹1,500 or more per month from another government financial assistance scheme
applicationMode: Online via Nari Shakti Doot App / ladkibahin.maharashtra.gov.in & Offline at Anganwadi Centres / Setu Suvidha Kendra
offlineProcess: Visit your local Anganwadi Centre, Gram Panchayat, Setu Suvidha Kendra, or Ward Office in municipal areas. Anganwadi workers assist women with online submission through their mobile phones free of cost.
commonMistakes: Bank account not mapped on NPCI: The payment bounces if the bank account is not actively mapped for Aadhaar DBT.
Age below 21 or above 65: The portal automatically checks birth year from Aadhaar and rejects out-of-range applicants.
Family member filing income tax: Auto-detected via tax department integration.
processingTime: Sanctioned within 15 to 30 days of verification.
renewalRequired: No monthly renewal needed; continuous monthly credits.
trackingProcedure: Log in to the Nari Shakti Doot app or ladkibahin.maharashtra.gov.in to check approval and disbursement status.
correctionProcedure: Anganwadi workers can unlock defective applications on the portal for document re-upload.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Woman's Bank Account via PFMS
disbursementDetails: Government of Maharashtra transfers ₹1,500 every month directly into the woman's Aadhaar-linked savings account.
helpline: Maharashtra Women Helpline: 181 / Ladki Bahin Call Centre: 022-22027050

name: MahaDBT Scholarships (Maharashtra)
department: Government of Maharashtra (multiple departments)
description: Single portal for Maharashtra's post-matric scholarships, fee reimbursement and freeships across departments.
whoCanApply: Maharashtra domicile students in post-matric courses; category and income limits differ by scheme (up to ₹8 lakh for some).
benefits: Full or partial college tuition and exam fee reimbursement (100% for SC/ST; 50% to 100% for OBC/VJNT/EBC) plus maintenance allowance up to ₹1,200/month (for hostellers) and Swadhar hostel scheme assistance up to ₹51,000/year for students unable to secure government hostel seats.
deadlineInfo: Announced annually: opens August/September and closes January/February.

process: Step 1: Visit mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in and click 'New Applicant Registration'.
Step 2: Enter Aadhaar Number and complete biometric or OTP verification.
Step 3: Create username and password. Complete Profile (Personal, Address, Caste, Income, and Bank details).
Step 4: Select 'Post Matric Scholarship' and choose your respective department (e.g. Social Justice / Tribal / OBC).
Step 5: Select your Course, Institute, CAP Allotment details, and upload fee receipt.
Step 6: Upload Caste Certificate, Caste Validity, Domicile, and Tahsildar Income Certificate.
Step 7: Submit the application and download the Application PDF.
Step 8: Submit the printout and verified document photocopies to your college scholarship desk.
Step 9: College verifies on portal (Level 1), District Assistant Commissioner approves (Level 2).
Step 10: Fee reimbursement is credited to college/student account, and maintenance allowance to student's bank account via PFMS.

faqs.q: What is the Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Shikshan Shulkh Shishyavrutti Yojna on MahaDBT?
faqs.a: This is the flagship EBC scheme providing 50% tuition fee and exam fee reimbursement to General/Open category students whose family income is less than ₹8,00,000 per year.

faqs.q: Is Caste Validity mandatory for all courses?
faqs.a: Caste Validity is mandatory for professional degree courses (Engineering, Medical, Architecture, Pharmacy, Law, MBA). For general courses (B.A., B.Sc., B.Com), Caste Certificate is sufficient.

faqs.q: What is the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Swadhar Yojana?
faqs.a: Swadhar provides up to ₹51,000 per year for food, lodging, and books to SC/Navbouddha students who do not get admission into government hostels.

faqs.q: Can students admitted through institute-level quota apply?
faqs.a: No, students admitted through management / institute quota are not eligible for government fee reimbursement.

faqs.q: What is the family income limit for OBC students?
faqs.a: For OBC post-matric scholarship, the income limit is ₹1,50,000 per year (for 100% fee waiver) and up to ₹8,00,000 (for 50% fee reimbursement under freeship).

faqs.q: How many times can I edit my MahaDBT form?
faqs.a: Once submitted, you can only edit if your college or district officer rejects it back to 'Sent Back' status.

purpose: MahaDBT (Aaple Sarkar DBT Portal) is the Maharashtra Government's comprehensive single-window scholarship portal integrating educational schemes across Social Justice, Tribal Development, VJNT/OBC/SBC, Higher & Technical Education, and Agriculture departments for automated fee reimbursement and scholarships.
targetBeneficiary: Students residing in Maharashtra belonging to SC, ST, VJNT, OBC, SBC, and EBC categories pursuing higher secondary, diploma, undergraduate, and postgraduate courses.
financialBenefit: 50% to 100% college tuition fee reimbursement + monthly maintenance allowance up to ₹1,200/month
benefitFrequency: Annual scholarship disbursed in two academic installments
impact: Automates educational fee waivers for over 25 lakh students annually across Maharashtra, preventing dropouts and ensuring transparency via Aadhaar DBT.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: No age limit for degree students.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: SC/ST: up to ₹2,50,000 per year; VJNT/OBC/SBC/EBC: up to ₹1,50,000 to ₹8,00,000 per year depending on specific sub-scheme.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Passed Class 10 or 12 and currently admitted to a recognized institution in Maharashtra.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: SC, ST, VJNT, OBC, SBC, SEBC, and EWS/EBC.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Not more than 2 beneficiaries per family.

mandatoryConditions: Must possess a Maharashtra Domicile Certificate
Must hold a valid Caste Certificate and Caste Validity Certificate (for professional courses)
Must have an authentic Income Certificate issued by Tahsildar / Revenue Authority
Student bank account must be actively seeded with Aadhaar on NPCI
conditionalRequirements: Caste Validity Certificate is mandatory for all professional degree courses (Engineering, Medical, MBA, Pharmacy, Law).
ineligibility: Non-domicile students of Maharashtra
Students admitted through management quota without centralized CAP counseling in professional courses
Family annual income exceeding category threshold
applicationMode: Online via MahaDBT Portal (mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in)
offlineProcess: Submit physical application printout along with attested photocopies of caste validity, domicile, income certificate, and fee receipt to your college scholarship clerk.
commonMistakes: Not having Caste Validity: Admission in professional courses like engineering or pharmacy without caste validity halts scholarship disbursement.
Uploading Form 16 instead of Tahsildar Income Certificate: MahaDBT strictly requires an official revenue certificate signed by the Tahsildar.
Aadhaar bank account inactive: Payment gets stuck if account has not transacted within 6 months.
processingTime: 60 to 90 days following college and district verification.
renewalRequired: Yes, students must log in and submit renewal applications each academic year.
trackingProcedure: Log in to mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in and click 'My Applied Schemes' to view status.
correctionProcedure: If application is sent back with remarks by college/district officer, edit and re-submit within 7 days.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Student / College Bank Account via PFMS
disbursementDetails: Tuition fees are disbursed directly to the college account or student account, and maintenance allowances are credited to the student's personal Aadhaar-linked savings account.

description: Pre-matric and post-matric scholarships and fee reimbursement for UP students across categories.
whoCanApply: Uttar Pradesh students; income limits depend on category (commonly ₹2–2.5 lakh).
benefits: Full reimbursement of university/college non-refundable tuition fees (up to ₹50,000+ per year) plus a monthly scholarship maintenance allowance credited directly into the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account.
deadlineInfo: Announced annually in phased schedules (usually July to November for Phase 1; December to January for Phase 2).
