process: Step 1: Visit scholarship.up.gov.in and click on 'Student' -> 'Registration'.
Step 2: Select your category (SC/ST/General, OBC, or Minority) and stage (Post-Matric Intermediate or Post-Matric Other Than Inter).
Step 3: Complete DigiLocker authentication: link your Aadhaar number to fetch verified identity details.
Step 4: Enter High School (Class 10) Board, Year of Passing, and Roll Number.
Step 5: Fill in Income Certificate Application Number & Certificate ID (system auto-verifies from e-District).
Step 6: Fill in Caste Certificate Application Number & Certificate ID.
Step 7: Enter College Name, Course, Non-Refundable Approved Fee amount, and Bank Account details.
Step 8: Review the draft form and make corrections before final submission.
Step 9: Click 'Final Submit' and print the official application form after 3 days.
Step 10: Submit the hardcopy and attested documents to your college for digital forwardal to the District Social Welfare Officer.

faqs.q: What is the family income limit for OBC and General students in UP?
faqs.a: The total annual family income from all sources must not exceed ₹2,00,000 per annum for General, OBC, and Minority students.

faqs.q: Can B.Tech and MBBS students get their full fees reimbursed?
faqs.a: Yes. For students admitted through merit counseling in government or recognized private colleges, the approved non-refundable tuition fee (up to ₹50,000+) is reimbursed.

faqs.q: What is the DigiLocker verification step on the UP portal?
faqs.a: Applicants must authenticate their DigiLocker account to electronically import verified Aadhaar and high school marksheet details, preventing fake registrations.

faqs.q: Can students studying outside Uttar Pradesh apply?
faqs.a: Only if enrolled in a central university or premier institution (like IITs/NITs) and holding a permanent UP domicile.

faqs.q: What should I do if my status says 'Blocked due to low attendance'?
faqs.a: Colleges must certify at least 75% biometric/digital attendance on the portal. Contact your college principal to verify your attendance record.

faqs.q: How can I check if my scholarship has been disbursed?
faqs.a: You can check status on scholarship.up.gov.in under 'Application Status' or track the transaction on the PFMS portal (pfms.nic.in) using 'Know Your Payment'.

purpose: The Uttar Pradesh Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement Online System (Saksham), managed by the Social Welfare, Backward Classes Welfare, and Minority Welfare departments of UP, provides comprehensive fee reimbursement and maintenance allowances to underprivileged students across Uttar Pradesh.
targetBeneficiary: Students residing in Uttar Pradesh belonging to SC, ST, OBC, General, and Minority categories studying in post-matric courses (Classes 11, 12, ITI, Polytechnic, Undergraduate, Postgraduate, and PhD).
financialBenefit: Full non-refundable college fees reimbursed + maintenance allowance up to ₹1,200/month
benefitFrequency: Annual single or two-stage disbursement via DBT
impact: Enables millions of rural and lower-income students across Uttar Pradesh to complete higher education, professional degrees, and technical polytechnics.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: No age limit for college students.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: SC/ST: up to ₹2,50,000 per year; General, OBC, Minority: up to ₹2,00,000 per year.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Passed previous qualifying exam and admitted to recognized course in UP (or select institutions outside UP).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: SC, ST, OBC, General, and Minorities.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Income verified via UP Revenue Portal.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a permanent resident / domicile of Uttar Pradesh
Annual family income must not exceed ₹2.5 Lakh (SC/ST) or ₹2.0 Lakh (OBC/General/Minority)
Must possess an authentic digital Income Certificate and Caste Certificate verifiable on the UP edistrict.up.gov.in portal
Must have completed DigiLocker Aadhaar verification on the UP scholarship portal
conditionalRequirements: Hosteller certificate required to claim higher maintenance allowance.
ineligibility: Non-UP domicile students
Family annual income exceeding category limits
Students failing in the preceding class (except where specific scheme rules permit)
Students admitted through management quota without merit counseling in private professional colleges
applicationMode: Online via UP Scholarship Portal (scholarship.up.gov.in)
offlineProcess: Students must submit the printed application hardcopy along with photocopies of all verified certificates to their college scholarship counter within 7 days of online submission.
commonMistakes: Aadhaar NPCI mapping missing: Payment fails if the bank account is not mapped to NPCI for Aadhaar-based DBT.
Mismatched High School Roll Number: The portal automatically verifies Class 10 records with UP Board/CBSE; any typo rejects the form.
Delayed college verification: Colleges must electronically forward forms before the official departmental cut-off date.
processingTime: Payment disbursed in scheduled tranches between December and March.
renewalRequired: Yes, students must select 'Renewal Login' on the portal for every subsequent year.
trackingProcedure: Click 'Status' on scholarship.up.gov.in and enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth to view complete verification progress.
correctionProcedure: Use the 'Correction Window' opened by the department in December/January to modify flagged errors.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Student's Bank Account via PFMS
disbursementDetails: Tuition fee reimbursement and monthly maintenance allowances are transferred in single/two installments directly into the student's Aadhaar-linked savings account.
helpline: UP Social Welfare Toll-Free: 1800-180-5131 / Backward Classes: 1800-180-5133

name: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (Uttar Pradesh)
department: Women Welfare Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh
description: Staged financial support for girls from birth through graduation in Uttar Pradesh.
whoCanApply: UP resident families with annual income up to ₹3 lakh, for up to two daughters.
benefits: Total financial grant of ₹25,000 (enhanced by the UP Government in 2024 from ₹15,000) disbursed across 6 developmental milestones: Stage 1: ₹5,000 at birth; Stage 2: ₹2,000 on complete vaccination; Stage 3: ₹3,000 on admission to Class 1; Stage 4: ₹3,000 on admission to Class 6; Stage 5: ₹5,000 on admission to Class 9; Stage 6: ₹7,000 on admission to degree or 2-year diploma course.
deadlineInfo: Stage 1 must be filed within 6 months of birth; Stage 2 within 1 year; school stages within 1 year of admission.

rules.label: Has a daughter (milestones start at birth)

documents.name: UP Domicile Certificate (Niwas Praman Patra)
documents.why: Confirms permanent residence in Uttar Pradesh.

documents.why: Verifies family meets economic criteria.

documents.why: Proves date of birth and parentage.

documents.why: Proves complete mandatory age-appropriate vaccinations.

documents.why: Proves active enrollment in Class 1, 6, 9, or college degree course.

documents.why: Identity verification and DBT.

documents.why: For receiving milestone DBT transfers.

process: Step 1: Visit mksy.up.gov.in and click 'Citizen Service Portal - Apply Here'.
Step 2: Read terms and click 'I Agree'. Register with Mobile Number and Name.
Step 3: Log in using your Login ID and Password.
Step 4: Register the Girl Child by providing her Name, Date of Birth, and Aadhaar.
Step 5: Select the appropriate Stage (Stage 1 to Stage 6) for which you are applying.
Step 6: Upload Domicile Certificate, Income Certificate, Birth Certificate, and relevant Stage proof (Vaccination card or School admission certificate).
Step 7: Provide Bank Account details (Mother's account or Joint account with daughter).
Step 8: Submit the application online. Print the acknowledgement slip.
Step 9: Block Development Officer (rural) or SDM (urban) verifies records.
Step 10: District Probation Officer (DPO) approves, and milestone funds are credited directly to the bank account via PFMS.

faqs.q: How much total money is given under Kanya Sumangala Yojana?
faqs.a: In 2024, the UP Government enhanced the total package from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per girl child across 6 milestones.

faqs.q: Can two daughters from the same family get this benefit?
faqs.a: Yes, up to two girl children from the same family can receive the full ₹25,000 benefit.

faqs.q: What are the 6 stages of assistance?
faqs.a: Stage 1: ₹5,000 at birth; Stage 2: ₹2,000 on vaccination; Stage 3: ₹3,000 in Class 1; Stage 4: ₹3,000 in Class 6; Stage 5: ₹5,000 in Class 9; Stage 6: ₹7,000 upon college admission.

faqs.q: Can I apply for Stage 3 directly if I missed Stage 1?
faqs.a: Yes! If a girl is currently studying in Class 1, Class 6, Class 9, or College, parents can apply directly for that specific milestone stage without having claimed earlier stages.

faqs.q: What is the family annual income limit?
faqs.a: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹3,00,000 per annum.

faqs.q: In whose bank account is the money credited?
faqs.a: For minor girls (Stages 1 to 5), money is credited to the mother's bank account (or joint account). For Stage 6 (college admission), it can be credited directly to the girl's own account.

purpose: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana, implemented by the Women and Child Development Department of Uttar Pradesh, provides conditional milestone-based financial assistance to girl children from birth through graduation, eliminating female feticide, promoting female education, and boosting the sex ratio.
targetBeneficiary: Girl children born in Uttar Pradesh whose family annual income is up to ₹3,00,000 per annum (maximum 2 girl children per family).
financialBenefit: Total financial grant of ₹25,000 disbursed across 6 developmental and educational milestones via DBT
benefitFrequency: Milestone-based stage disbursements from birth through college graduation
impact: Prevents female infanticide, ensures 100% infant immunization, eliminates high school dropouts among girls, and enables completion of university graduation.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Girl child from birth up to completion of graduation.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Total family annual income must NOT exceed ₹3,00,000 per annum.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories in Uttar Pradesh.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Permanent resident / domicile of Uttar Pradesh.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Maximum of two girl children per family (up to three permitted in case of twin girls on second delivery).

mandatoryConditions: Family must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh
Total family annual income must not exceed ₹3,00,000 per year
Maximum of two girl children per family are eligible
Mother or father must possess an Aadhaar-seeded bank account for minor girl child (or girl's own account for Stage 6)
conditionalRequirements: Twin girl birth certificate allows exemption to cover a third daughter.
ineligibility: Families with annual income exceeding ₹3,00,000
Families with more than two living children (unless twins were born in the second delivery)
Non-UP domicile families
applicationMode: Online via MKSY Portal (mksy.up.gov.in) or Offline via Block Development Office / CDPO
offlineProcess: Submit physical application form along with verified document copies to your local Block Development Office (BDO), Child Development Project Officer (CDPO), or District Probation Officer (DPO).
commonMistakes: Applying for Stage 1 after 6 months of birth: Stage 1 application must be submitted within 6 months of the girl child's birth.
Missing vaccination record for Stage 2: Must complete all primary immunizations (BCG, OPV, DPT, Measles) within 1 year.
Family income exceeding ₹3 Lakh: The system cross-verifies with the state e-District portal and rejects ineligible forms.
processingTime: Sanctioned within 45 to 60 days of submission.
renewalRequired: Fresh milestone application required at each of the 6 stages.
trackingProcedure: Log in to mksy.up.gov.in and check 'Application Status' on the citizen dashboard.
correctionProcedure: DPO can mark defective for online document re-upload.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Mother / Girl's Bank Account via PFMS
disbursementDetails: Milestone funds (from ₹2,000 to ₹7,000) are credited directly into the mother's (or girl child's) savings account upon stage verification.

name: Kanyashree Prakalpa (West Bengal)
department: Department of Women & Child Development, Government of West Bengal
applyChannel: your school / college Kanyashree nodal officer
description: Conditional cash transfer to keep adolescent girls in education and delay marriage.
whoCanApply: Unmarried girls aged 13–19 studying in Class 8 or above in West Bengal, with family income up to ₹1.2 lakh (condition relaxed for some categories).
benefits: Two-tiered conditional cash assistance: K1 Annual Scholarship of ₹1,000 per year for unmarried girls aged 13 to 18 studying in Classes 8 to 12; K2 One-Time Grant of ₹25,000 paid to the girl upon turning 18, provided she remains unmarried and continues her education in college, university, or vocational training.
deadlineInfo: K1 applications open in September/October; K2 applications accepted continuously upon turning 18.

documents.issuingAuthority: Self & Parent declaration countersigned by School/College Principal

documents.why: Verifies date of birth and age requirement.

documents.name: School / College Bonafide Certificate
documents.why: Confirms active enrollment in recognized educational institution.

documents.why: For receiving direct DBT cash transfers.

process: Step 1: Collect Kanyashree Form (Form K1 for school students; Form K2 upon turning 18) from your school/college office.
Step 2: Fill in personal details, birth date, and bank account details.
Step 3: Attach Birth Certificate, Aadhaar Card, Bank Passbook, and Unmarried Declaration.
Step 4: Submit the completed form to your School Headmaster or College Nodal Teacher.
Step 5: School teacher uploads details and documents onto the official wbkanyashree.gov.in portal.
Step 6: Unique Kanyashree ID is generated for the student.
Step 7: Block Development Officer (BDO) / Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) conducts electronic approval.
Step 8: K1 (₹1,000) or K2 (₹25,000) is credited directly into the girl's bank account via online treasury.
Step 9: Student receives SMS confirmation on her mobile phone upon credit.

faqs.q: Is there any family income limit for Kanyashree?
faqs.a: No! The Government of West Bengal made Kanyashree universal. There is NO family income ceiling.

faqs.q: Can a girl who is married get the ₹25,000 K2 grant?
faqs.a: No. The core objective of the scheme is delaying child marriage. The girl must be strictly unmarried at the time of receiving the K2 grant.

faqs.q: What is K3 in Kanyashree?
faqs.a: K3 is an extension for postgraduate university studies, providing ₹2,500/month for Science streams and ₹2,000/month for Arts/Commerce streams to Kanyashree scholars who passed graduation with 45% marks.

faqs.q: Can students in madrasahs and vocational schools apply?
faqs.a: Yes, students of recognized madrasahs, vocational training centres, and polytechnics are fully eligible.

faqs.q: Can the ₹25,000 grant be used for college admission?
faqs.a: Yes, the K2 grant is completely unconditional cash that the girl can use for university admission, competitive coaching, laptop purchase, or personal savings.

faqs.q: What happens if my bank account changed?
faqs.a: Inform your school/college Kanyashree nodal teacher immediately with a photocopy of your new passbook so they can update the portal before disbursement.

purpose: Kanyashree Prakalpa, a United Nations Public Service Award-winning flagship initiative of the Government of West Bengal, prevents child marriage and keeps adolescent girls in school through conditional cash scholarships, delaying marriage until at least age 18.
targetBeneficiary: Unmarried adolescent girls residing in West Bengal studying in government or recognized schools, colleges, or universities.
financialBenefit: K1: ₹1,000 annual scholarship (Classes 8–12) + K2: ₹25,000 one-time grant upon attaining 18 years while unmarried
benefitFrequency: Annual (K1) and One-Time Lump Sum (K2)
impact: Dramatically reduced child marriage rates across West Bengal, increased female secondary and college enrolment, and empowered millions of young women to pursue career aspirations.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: K1: 13 to 18 years; K2: 18 to 19 years.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO family income ceiling (the income barrier was completely removed by the West Bengal Government to make Kanyashree universal).
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Enrolled in recognized school, college, madrasah, or vocational institute.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all castes and religions.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Must be strictly unmarried on the date of application.

mandatoryConditions: Must be an unmarried girl student studying in an institution in West Bengal
For K1: Must be between 13 and 18 years and enrolled in Class 8 to 12
For K2: Must have completed 18 years (and below 19) and remain strictly unmarried
Must hold an individual bank account in her own name
conditionalRequirements: Special disability exemption: Girls with 40%+ disability can receive K1 even below Class 8.
ineligibility: Girls married before attaining 18 years of age (strictly disqualified from K2 grant)
Girls who have dropped out of educational institutions
Male students
applicationMode: Through School / College Kanyashree Portal (wbkanyashree.gov.in)
offlineProcess: Students do not need to visit government offices. The entire registration and upload process is managed inside schools, colleges, and madrasahs across West Bengal by designated Kanyashree teachers.
commonMistakes: Getting married before 18: If a girl marries before completing 18 years, she is permanently disqualified from receiving the ₹25,000 K2 grant.
Opening bank account with parent joint signature: Account must strictly be in the girl student's own individual name.
Failing to submit K2 within 18–19 years: K2 application must be submitted during the year she is 18.
processingTime: Payment disbursed within 30 to 45 days of institutional verification.
renewalRequired: K1 renewed annually in school; K2 is a one-time grant.
trackingProcedure: Track application status on wbkanyashree.gov.in using your 20-digit Kanyashree ID.
correctionProcedure: School/college nodal officer can edit rejected student data on the portal.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into Girl Student's Bank Account via WB IFMS
disbursementDetails: West Bengal Department of Women & Child Development transfers funds directly from state treasury into the girl's individual bank account.

name: Swasthya Sathi (West Bengal)
department: Department of Health & Family Welfare, Government of West Bengal
description: Family health cover for West Bengal residents, with the card issued in the name of the senior woman of the family.
whoCanApply: West Bengal families not covered by other government health schemes.
benefits: Basic health cover up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation across 2,000+ empanelled government and private hospitals in West Bengal and select premier multi-speciality hospitals nationwide.
deadlineInfo: Universal ongoing scheme. New cards issued at all Duare Sarkar camps and BDO offices.

rules.label: Not covered by another government health insurance scheme

process: Step 1: Fill out Application Form B during the statewide 'Duare Sarkar' (Government at your Doorstep) camps or at the local BDO office.
Step 2: Enter family details with the eldest female member as the Head of Household.
Step 3: Provide Aadhaar and Khadya Sathi Digital Ration Card numbers for all family members.
Step 4: Visit the camp's biometric photography counter for photograph and fingerprint capture.
Step 5: The physical biometric Swasthya Sathi Smart Card is printed and handed over on the spot.
Step 6: Show the card at the Swasthya Sathi desk of any empanelled hospital for cashless admission.

faqs.q: Is Swasthya Sathi valid in private hospitals outside West Bengal?
faqs.a: Yes. Swasthya Sathi has empanelled select premier multi-speciality hospitals in other states, including Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore, Tamil Nadu.

faqs.q: Can men use the Swasthya Sathi card?
faqs.a: Yes. Even though the card is issued in the name of the female head of household, all family members (husband, sons, father, in-laws) listed on the card receive the full ₹5 Lakh cover.

faqs.q: Is there any income limit to get a Swasthya Sathi card?
faqs.a: No. The scheme is universal across West Bengal for all citizens not receiving government medical allowance.

faqs.q: What should I do if a private hospital refuses to accept the card?
faqs.a: Immediately call the Swasthya Sathi 24/7 Toll-Free Helpline at 1800-345-5384. Swasthya Sathi nodal officers are assigned to all network hospitals.

faqs.q: Are pre-existing diseases covered?
faqs.a: Yes, all pre-existing medical conditions are covered from day one without waiting periods.

faqs.q: How much does the card cost?
faqs.a: The Swasthya Sathi Smart Card is completely free of cost.

purpose: Swasthya Sathi was launched by the Government of West Bengal to provide universal healthcare financial protection to the entire population of West Bengal, empowering female heads of households with smart card-based health security.
targetBeneficiary: All families residing in West Bengal, with the Smart Health Card issued in the name of the eldest female member of the family.
financialBenefit: Cashless hospitalisation coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year
benefitFrequency: Annual floating family coverage
impact: Universal healthcare without out-of-pocket medical expenditure, pioneering women's empowerment by designating the mother/grandmother as cardholder.

detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: Card issued in the name of the eldest female member; benefits cover all male and female family members.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: NO income restriction (Universal coverage across West Bengal).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Open to all occupations (except government servants receiving medical allowance).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: All castes and categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Parents, spouse, children, and dependent in-laws of the female head of household.

Must possess an official Swasthya Sathi Smart Card issued by the state government
Must seek admission in an empanelled public or private network hospital
conditionalRequirements: Pre-authorisation required for non-emergency elective procedures.
ineligibility: State and Central Government employees and pensioners receiving regular medical allowances from the government
Families already covered under government employee health schemes like WBHS
applicationMode: Offline at 'Duare Sarkar' Camps / BDO Office or Online at data.swasthyasathi.gov.in
offlineProcess: Visit your local Block Development Office (BDO) or attend the regular Duare Sarkar camps organized across municipal wards and gram panchayats in West Bengal.
commonMistakes: Applying with male member as primary head: The card is legally issued in the name of the eldest female member of the family.
Not carrying the physical card to hospital: Hospitals require swiping the physical chip card on their terminal.
processingTime: Same-day card issuance at Duare Sarkar camps; pre-authorization within 1 to 2 hours at hospital.
renewalRequired: Auto-renews annually on 1st April without paperwork.
trackingProcedure: Check your card URN status on swasthyasathi.gov.in under 'Find Your Name'.
correctionProcedure: Submit Form C (member addition/deletion) at the local BDO / Municipal office.
disbursementMethod: 100% Cashless Inpatient Hospitalisation Settlement
disbursementDetails: Hospital swipes the Swasthya Sathi card, locks the package amount, and receives direct payment from the West Bengal Swasthya Sathi Trust via online portal.

name: Lakshmir Bhandar (West Bengal)
department: Department of Women & Child Development, Government of West Bengal
description: Monthly basic income support for women heads of West Bengal households.
whoCanApply: Women aged 25–60 residing in West Bengal with a Swasthya Sathi card, who are not permanent government employees or pensioners.
benefits: Direct unconditional monthly cash transfer: ₹1,200 per month for SC/ST women (enhanced in 2024 from ₹1,000) and ₹1,000 per month for General/OBC women (enhanced in 2024 from ₹500) transferred directly into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. Upon attaining 60 years, beneficiaries transition automatically to the state Old Age Pension at the same rate.
deadlineInfo: Accepted at all Duare Sarkar camps throughout the year.
