department: Medical, Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Rajasthan
targetBeneficiary: All families residing in Rajasthan holding Jan Aadhaar Cards
description: Universal cashless health insurance scheme providing coverage up to ₹25,00,000 per family per year, plus ₹5 Lakh accidental cover, for treatments at 1,800+ empanelled hospitals.
detailedDescription: Rajasthan's Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya (Chiranjeevi) Yojana is India's most expansive state-level universal health assurance scheme. Offering an unprecedented health cover of up to ₹25,00,000 per family per year, it covers all secondary and tertiary inpatient procedures, organ transplants (heart, liver, bone marrow, kidney), cancer care, ICU, dialysis, and neurosurgeries. It is 100% free for NFSA, BPL, SECC, small farmers, and contractual workers, and accessible to any other family for an annual premium of just ₹850.
purpose: Guarantees universal health coverage so no family in Rajasthan suffers financial ruin from major illness, supporting SDG 3.
benefits: Cashless secondary and tertiary hospital treatment up to ₹25 Lakh per family per year across 1,800+ government and private hospitals, plus ₹5 Lakh accidental insurance cover.
financialBenefit: Cashless health cover up to ₹25,00,000 per family/year + ₹5,00,000 accidental cover
benefitFrequency: Annual floating coverage per family
impact: Has delivered free life-saving cardiac surgeries, organ transplants, and oncology therapies to over 40 lakh patients in Rajasthan.
specificAdvantages: Pre-existing diseases covered from day one; covers expensive organ transplants and modern cancer therapies completely cashlessly.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Free category: NFSA, BPL, small farmers, contractual workers. Paid category: All other citizens for ₹850/year.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of Rajasthan holding a Jan Aadhaar Card.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: No cap on family size or age.

mandatoryConditions: Must possess an active Jan Aadhaar Card issued by the Government of Rajasthan
Treatment must be at an empanelled government or private network hospital
Families not in the free category must pay the subsidized ₹850 annual premium
ineligibility: State and Central Government employees covered under Rajasthan Government Health Scheme (RGHS) or CGHS

documents.name: Rajasthan Jan Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Mandatory primary identification for all state schemes.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card of Family Members
documents.why: Biometric e-KYC authentication.

applicationMode: Online via chiranjeevi.rajasthan.gov.in & Offline via e-Mitra kiosks
process: Step 1: Check your Jan Aadhaar Card status on janaadhaar.rajasthan.gov.in.
Step 2: Visit chiranjeevi.rajasthan.gov.in or your local e-Mitra kiosk.
Step 3: Enter your Jan Aadhaar number; eligible free categories are auto-verified.
Step 4: Non-free families pay the subsidized ₹850 annual premium online.
Step 5: Policy activates instantly.
Step 6: When admitted to any empanelled hospital, show your Jan Aadhaar Card at the Chiranjeevi Help Desk for instant cashless pre-authorization.
offlineProcess: Walk into any of the 85,000+ e-Mitra service kiosks across Rajasthan with your Jan Aadhaar card.
commonMistakes: Not adding all family members to the Jan Aadhaar card before hospitalization.
Forgetting to renew the ₹850 annual premium on the portal for non-NFSA families.
processingTime: Immediate policy activation; pre-authorization at hospital desk within 1 hour
renewalRequired: Annual renewal for paid category (automatic for NFSA/BPL families)
trackingProcedure: Search Jan Aadhaar ID on chiranjeevi.rajasthan.gov.in to verify active policy status.
correctionProcedure: Add missing family members or update mobile numbers on the Jan Aadhaar portal at any e-Mitra kiosk.
disbursementMethod: 100% Cashless Treatment at Hospital Desk via State Health Agency TMS
disbursementDetails: Hospital submits digital claims to Rajasthan State Health Agency. All surgery, doctor fees, ICU, implants, diagnostics, and medicines are paid directly to the hospital.

faqs.q: Are organ transplants covered?
faqs.a: Yes. Heart, liver, kidney, and bone marrow transplants are covered up to the ₹25 Lakh limit.

faqs.q: Can families who are not poor join?
faqs.a: Yes. Any resident of Rajasthan can enroll by paying just ₹850 per year per family.

name: KALIA Scheme (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation - Odisha)
title: KALIA Scheme (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation - Odisha)
department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Empowerment, Government of Odisha
targetBeneficiary: Small and marginal farmers, tenant cultivators (sharecroppers), and landless agricultural laborers in Odisha
description: Financial assistance of ₹10,000 per year for small/marginal farmers and ₹12,500 livelihood package for landless farm laborers, plus ₹2 Lakh life and accident insurance cover.
detailedDescription: KALIA is recognized nationally for including landless agricultural laborers and sharecroppers alongside landowners. Under KALIA, small and marginal farmers receive ₹10,000 per year (₹4,000 in Kharif, ₹4,000 in Rabi, and top-up) directly into bank accounts via DBT for purchasing seeds and fertilizers. Crucially, landless agricultural households receive a financial livelihood package of ₹12,500 to establish goat rearing, poultry, duckery, or bee-keeping units, alongside interest-free crop loans up to ₹1,00,000.
purpose: Accelerates agricultural prosperity, eliminates rural poverty, and supports tenant farmers and landless laborers with dignified livelihood capital, supporting SDG 1 and SDG 2.
benefits: ₹10,000/year farm input assistance for cultivators; ₹12,500 livelihood package for landless households; 0% interest crop loans up to ₹1 Lakh; and free life insurance cover of ₹2 Lakh.
financialBenefit: ₹10,000/year (Farmers) or ₹12,500 livelihood package (Landless) + 0% interest crop loan
benefitFrequency: Seasonal DBT installments (Kharif and Rabi)
impact: Over 50 lakh small farmers and landless families empowered, transforming rural household incomes across western and coastal Odisha.
specificAdvantages: Explicitly protects sharecroppers and landless rural laborers who own no registered farmland.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit for small/marginal farmers and landless laborers.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Small/marginal farmer, tenant cultivator (sharecropper), or landless agricultural laborer.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: One benefit per household.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a resident of Odisha cultivating land or working as an agricultural laborer
Aadhaar-seeded savings bank account
Inclusion in the Gram Panchayat KALIA beneficiary list
ineligibility: Large farmers owning more than 5 acres of land
Government employees, pensioners, and income tax payers

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Biometric identification and de-duplication.

documents.name: Ration Card (NFSA / SFSS)
documents.why: Confirms family composition.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Seeded Bank Passbook
documents.why: For receiving direct cash DBT.

documents.name: Land Record / Sharecropper Declaration
documents.why: Proves farming or tenant status.

applicationMode: Online via kalia.odisha.gov.in & Offline via Mo Seva Kendra / Gram Panchayat office
process: Step 1: Check your name in the Gram Panchayat KALIA draft list displayed at your GP office.
Step 2: If name is missing, apply online at kalia.odisha.gov.in under 'New Application'.
Step 3: Enter your Aadhaar, Ration card number, and bank account details.
Step 4: Village Agriculture Worker (VAW) and Gram Panchayat committee conduct field verification.
Step 5: District Committee clears the final beneficiary list.
Step 6: Financial assistance is credited directly into the farmer's bank account via DBT.
offlineProcess: Submit application at your Gram Panchayat office or nearest Mo Seva Kendra.
commonMistakes: Bank account not mapped to Aadhaar, preventing seasonal DBT credit.
Large farmers attempting to claim small farmer status.
openingDate: Continuous year-round grievance and enrollment windows
processingTime: Seasonal release aligned with crop sowing periods
renewalRequired: Automatic seasonal continuation
trackingProcedure: Track beneficiary payment status on kalia.odisha.gov.in > 'Track Beneficiary'.
correctionProcedure: Submit an online e-KYC / bank update request on the KALIA portal.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) via Odisha State Treasury to Bank Account
disbursementDetails: Transferred electronically directly to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

faqs.q: Can landless laborers apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Landless agricultural households receive the special ₹12,500 livelihood package for allied agricultural activities.

name: Orunodoi 2.0 Scheme (Assam)
title: Orunodoi 2.0 Scheme (Assam)
department: Finance Department, Government of Assam
targetBeneficiary: Female head of economically vulnerable and low-income households in Assam
description: Assam's flagship direct benefit cash transfer scheme providing ₹1,250 per month deposited directly into the bank accounts of 27+ lakh women heads of poor households on the 10th of every month.
detailedDescription: Orunodoi (Arunodoi 2.0) is the largest direct cash transfer welfare scheme in Northeast India. Operating on the principle of women-centric financial empowerment, it deposits ₹1,250 on the 10th of every calendar month straight into the savings bank account of the designated woman head of the family. The financial assistance covers basic medicines (₹400), pulses/sugar (₹400), fruits and vegetables (₹150), essential groceries (₹150), and electricity subsidy (₹150).
purpose: Eliminates household poverty, empowers women as the financial decision makers of the family, and supports nutritional sustenance, directly advancing SDG 1, SDG 2, and SDG 5.
benefits: Direct monthly cash grant of ₹1,250 deposited straight via DBT into the woman's bank account on the 10th of every month.
financialBenefit: ₹1,250 per month (₹15,000 annually) direct cash assistance to female head of household
benefitFrequency: Monthly Direct Benefit Transfer (on the 10th of every month)
impact: Over 27 lakh low-income families in Assam receive guaranteed monthly liquidity, significantly improving maternal nutrition and health.
specificAdvantages: Money belongs exclusively to the woman; cannot be attached by banks or diverted by family members.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Annual family income must not exceed ₹2,00,000.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (special priority to widows, divorced women, unmarried women, and households with disabled members).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Designated woman must hold an active savings bank account.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a permanent resident female of Assam aged 18 or above
Total family annual income below ₹2,00,000
Bank account must be in the name of the woman applicant and seeded with Aadhaar
ineligibility: Households with any family member who is a regular government employee or doctor, engineer, CA, architect
Households owning a four-wheeler motorized vehicle or mechanized tractor
Families owning more than 15 bighas of agricultural land

documents.name: Aadhaar Card of Female Applicant
documents.why: Mandatory biometric e-KYC.

documents.name: Ration Card (NFSA)
documents.why: Confirms family composition.

documents.name: Income Certificate (Below ₹2 Lakh)
documents.why: Proves income eligibility.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Seeded Bank Passbook in Woman's Name
documents.why: For monthly ₹1,250 DBT credit.

applicationMode: Doorstep survey by VCDC / Gaon Panchayat & Online via orunodoi.assam.gov.in
process: Step 1: Gaon Panchayat / VCDC officials conduct physical verification of eligible households in the village.
Step 2: The female applicant fills out the Orunodoi application proforma.
Step 3: Attach Aadhaar, Ration card, Income proof, and bank passbook.
Step 4: District Level Monitoring Committee (DLMC) headed by the Deputy Commissioner scrutinizes the beneficiary roster.
Step 5: Approved lists are published, and ₹1,250 is credited into the woman's bank account on the 10th of every month.
offlineProcess: Meet your Gaonburah (village headman) or Gaon Panchayat Secretary in rural areas, or Ward Commissioner in urban areas.
commonMistakes: Providing a joint bank account or husband's bank account (account MUST be exclusively in the woman's name).
Bank account not mapped in the NPCI mapper.
openingDate: Annual revision and enrollment drives notified by Finance Department
processingTime: 30 to 45 days following DLMC approval
renewalRequired: Periodic biometric re-verification by Orunodoi Sahayaks
trackingProcedure: Track beneficiary payment status on orunodoi.assam.gov.in using application number or mobile.
correctionProcedure: Contact your District Development Commissioner or Gaon Panchayat secretary.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) via Assam State Treasury to Bank Account
disbursementDetails: Transferred electronically directly to the woman's Aadhaar-linked savings account on Orunodoi Day (10th of each month).

faqs.q: Can a family with a disabled member get priority?
faqs.a: Yes. Families with divyangjan (disabled members) and widows receive top priority under Orunodoi.

name: Delhi Ladli Scheme
title: Delhi Ladli Scheme
department: Department of Women and Child Development, Government of NCT of Delhi
targetBeneficiary: Girl children born in low-income families residing in Delhi
description: Staged financial assistance totaling ₹35,000 to ₹36,000 deposited in the girl child's name with SBI Life Insurance, maturing to ₹1,00,000+ upon passing Class 12 at age 18.
detailedDescription: The Delhi Ladli Scheme enhances the social status of girl children in the National Capital Territory. Financial deposits are made at 6 vital milestones in the girl child's life: ₹11,000 at institutional birth (or ₹10,000 for home birth), ₹5,000 at admission to Class 1, ₹5,000 at Class 6, ₹5,000 at Class 9, ₹5,000 at Class 10, and ₹5,000 at Class 12. The accumulated funds compound in SBI Life Insurance and are paid as a lump-sum maturity exceeding ₹1 Lakh upon the girl completing Class 12 at age 18.
purpose: Eliminates sex-selective discrimination, promotes institutional births, prevents school dropouts among girl students, and secures financial independence, supporting SDG 5.
benefits: Staged deposits of ₹35,000 to ₹36,000 compounding to a guaranteed maturity payout exceeding ₹1,00,000 when the girl passes Class 12 at age 18.
financialBenefit: Milestone deposits totaling ₹36,000 maturing to ₹1,00,000+ at age 18
benefitFrequency: Milestone deposits at Birth, Class 1, 6, 9, 10, and 12
impact: Has fostered high school completion for girl students across Delhi slums and low-income urban settlements.
specificAdvantages: Funds cannot be withdrawn by parents or guardians early; strictly protected for the girl's college education or enterprise at age 18.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 0 to 18 years (enrolled at birth or upon school admission).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Annual family income must not exceed ₹1,00,000.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Must study in a recognized school in Delhi.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.residenceRequirement: Resident of Delhi for at least 3 continuous years.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Restricted to up to two girl children per family.

mandatoryConditions: Girl child must be born in Delhi and parents must have resided in Delhi for at least 3 years prior to application
Annual family income must be below ₹1,00,000
Girl must be enrolled in a recognized government, municipal, or aided school in Delhi
Girl must not marry before age 18 and must appear in Class 12 examinations
ineligibility: Third girl child born after notification date
Families whose annual income exceeds ₹1,00,000
Girl students dropping out before Class 12

documents.name: Child Birth Certificate
documents.why: Proof of girl child birth in Delhi.

documents.name: 3-Year Delhi Residence Proof (Voter ID / Ration Card / Electricity Bill)
documents.why: Proves 3 years residence in Delhi.

documents.name: Income Certificate (Below ₹1 Lakh)
documents.why: Confirms income eligibility.

documents.name: School Admission / Enrollment Certificate
documents.why: Verifies school milestones (Class 1, 6, 9, 10, 12).

applicationMode: Online via e-District Delhi (edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in) & at recognized Delhi Government Schools
process: Step 1: Obtain a 3-year residence proof and income certificate from e-District Delhi.
Step 2: For school-stage deposits, apply directly through the girl's school principal (nodal teacher).
Step 3: School uploads the enrollment and academic records to the Ladli portal.
Step 4: Department of WCD approves the deposit and credits funds to SBI Life Insurance.
Step 5: Collect the Ladli Deposit Certificate.
Step 6: On completing Class 12 at age 18, submit maturity claim to SBI Life Insurance with Class 12 marksheet.
offlineProcess: For school-going girls, submit application through the Ladli Teacher In-Charge at your government school. For newborns, submit at the District WCD Office.
commonMistakes: Failing to renew applications at each educational milestone (Class 1, 6, 9, 10, 12).
Income certificate expired at the time of renewal.
openingDate: Open throughout the academic year in schools
processingTime: 30 to 45 days for deposit registration
renewalRequired: Application renewal required at each milestone class
trackingProcedure: Track status on edistrict.delhigovt.nic.in using application number.
correctionProcedure: Contact School Ladli In-Charge or District WCD Officer.
disbursementMethod: Maturity payment transferred directly into girl's savings account by SBI Life
disbursementDetails: Lump-sum maturity paid directly via NEFT into the girl's individual bank account upon turning 18 and clearing Class 12.

faqs.q: What happens if the girl fails Class 12?
faqs.a: The girl must pass Class 10 and appear in Class 12 to claim maturity funds on turning 18.

name: MUMKIN Scheme (Mission Youth - Jammu & Kashmir)
title: MUMKIN Scheme (Mission Youth - Jammu & Kashmir)
department: Mission Youth, Government of Jammu & Kashmir
targetBeneficiary: Unemployed youth aged 18 to 35 in Jammu & Kashmir seeking commercial transport livelihoods
description: Commercial vehicle livelihood scheme providing 100% on-road down-payment subsidy (₹1,60,000+ government grant + matching vehicle manufacturer discount) for youth purchasing small commercial vehicles.
detailedDescription: MUMKIN is a celebrated youth livelihood program launched under J&K Mission Youth to establish sustainable self-employment in the transport sector. Unemployed youth receive customized commercial small load carriers (such as Tata Ace, Mahindra Bolero Maxi Truck, Ashok Leyland Dost, or commercial passenger vehicles) with zero personal down payment. Mission Youth contributes 10% of the on-road price (up to ₹80,000), the vehicle manufacturer provides a matching 10% cash discount (up to ₹80,000), making a combined 20% down payment (₹1.6 Lakh+), with J&K Bank financing the remaining 80%.
purpose: Transforms unemployed youth into self-reliant transport entrepreneurs, expands freight mobility across hilly terrain, and drives economic normalcy, supporting SDG 8.
benefits: Zero upfront down payment: 10% state grant + 10% manufacturer discount (₹1,60,000+ total upfront relief) + commercial vehicle delivery + fast-track commercial permit.
financialBenefit: Upfront capital subsidy of ₹1,60,000+ (Zero personal down-payment)
benefitFrequency: One-time vehicle livelihood grant
impact: Over 8,500 small commercial vehicles distributed to youth across border and remote districts, creating dignified independent earnings.
specificAdvantages: No margin money required from the youth; vehicle delivered on-road with permit, insurance, and fitness certificates.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Applicant must not already own a commercial vehicle.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a Domicile of Jammu and Kashmir aged between 18 and 35 years
Must possess a valid Driving License (LMV / Commercial)
Must be registered with the District Employment & Counseling Centre as unemployed
Must have a clear credit history for bank loan approval
ineligibility: Individuals already employed in government or formal private sector
Existing owners of commercial transport vehicles

documents.name: J&K Domicile Certificate
documents.why: Proof of permanent domicile.

documents.name: Driving License (LMV / Commercial)
documents.why: Confirms driving competency.

documents.name: Unemployment Certificate / District Employment Registration
documents.why: Proves unemployed status.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card & Bank Account Details
documents.why: Identity and bank financing.

applicationMode: Online via J&K Single Window Services (services.jk.gov.in) & District Employment Centres
process: Step 1: Visit services.jk.gov.in and click on 'Mission Youth - MUMKIN Scheme'.
Step 2: Enter Aadhaar, Domicile certificate, and Driving License details.
Step 3: Select your preferred vehicle model (Tata, Mahindra, Ashok Leyland, Maruti Commercial).
Step 4: District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) chaired by the Deputy Commissioner reviews applications.
Step 5: J&K Bank sanctions loan for 80% cost; Mission Youth and auto manufacturer deposit 20% down payment.
Step 6: Vehicle is delivered to the candidate with registration, permit, and fitness.
Step 7: Candidate operates the vehicle and repays monthly EMI from transport earnings.
offlineProcess: Visit your District Employment and Counseling Centre (DE&CC) in your district headquarters.
commonMistakes: Applying without a valid Driving License.
Defaulted credit score with J&K Bank or other financial institutions.
openingDate: Open year-round with periodic monthly DLTFC review meetings
processingTime: 30 to 45 business days from application to vehicle key delivery
renewalRequired: One-time scheme
trackingProcedure: Track application status on services.jk.gov.in or at the District Employment Centre.
correctionProcedure: Contact District Employment Officer (Mission Youth Nodal Officer).
disbursementMethod: Direct credit of 20% down payment to vehicle dealer / J&K Bank
disbursementDetails: Mission Youth subsidy and manufacturer discount credited directly into the loan account; vehicle delivered on-road to the applicant.

faqs.q: Is any personal down payment money required?
faqs.a: No. The entire 20% down payment is jointly borne by Mission Youth (10%) and the vehicle manufacturer (10%).

name: SHRESHTA Scheme (Residential Education for High School Students in Targeted Areas)
title: SHRESHTA Scheme (Residential Education for High School Students in Targeted Areas)
department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
targetBeneficiary: Meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) students studying in Class 8 and Class 10
description: 100% government-funded residential schooling in India's top CBSE private residential schools for meritorious SC students, covering full school fees, hostel fees, and mess charges.
detailedDescription: SHRESHTA provides high-quality residential education to meritorious Scheduled Caste students from poor backgrounds. Around 3,000 students are selected annually through the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA). Selected students are admitted into Class 9 and Class 11 in top-ranking private residential schools across India, with the Central Government covering all tuition fees, hostel expenses, uniforms, books, and mess fees up to Class 12.
purpose: Bridges the educational quality gap for marginalized Dalit students by granting access to elite CBSE residential schools, supporting SDG 4 and SDG 10.
benefits: 100% free education in top CBSE residential schools (school fee, hostel, mess, books, uniform up to ₹1,35,000 per student per year paid by the Central Government).
financialBenefit: Full scholarship up to ₹1,35,000/year (covering 100% school, hostel & mess charges)
benefitFrequency: Annual recurring scholarship through Class 12 completion
impact: Enables thousands of underprivileged SC students from rural and small-town backgrounds to enter premier IITs, AIIMS, and national universities.
specificAdvantages: No out-of-pocket costs for poor families; government reimburses schools directly through DBT/e-grant mode.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: Class 9 entry: Born between 01-04-2007 and 31-03-2011; Class 11 entry: Born between 01-04-2005 and 31-03-2009.
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Annual parental income from all sources must not exceed ₹2,50,000.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Currently studying in Class 8 (for admission in Class 9) or Class 10 (for admission in Class 11).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Scheduled Caste (SC) community only.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Must qualify in the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS).

Family annual income below ₹2,50,000 per year
Must appear and qualify in the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) conducted by NTA
ineligibility: Non-SC category students
Students whose parental income exceeds ₹2.5 Lakh/year

documents.name: Income Certificate (Below ₹2.5 Lakh)
documents.why: Confirms income ceiling.

documents.name: Class 8 / Class 10 Marksheet & Bonafide Certificate
documents.why: Academic qualification proof.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Biometric student identification.

applicationMode: 100% Online via NTA Portal (shreshta.nta.nic.in)
process: Step 1: Visit shreshta.nta.nic.in when annual NETS exam registration opens in February/March.
Step 2: Register online and fill the NETS application form with academic details and caste certificate.
Step 3: Download admit card and appear for the computer-based entrance examination.
Step 4: NTA declares all-India merit list based on test scores.
Step 5: Attend online web-counselling and select preferred top CBSE residential schools.
Step 6: School verifies documents and admits student into Class 9 or 11 with 100% free boarding and education.
offlineProcess: Online application through NTA portal only. School principals and CSC centres assist students with online filing.
commonMistakes: Missing the NTA exam application deadline in March.
Income certificate not issued in the name of the parent.
openingDate: Annual entrance exam registration opens in February/March each year
processingTime: Entrance exam held in May; school admissions completed by July
renewalRequired: Automatic continuation from Class 9 to 12 upon securing passing marks
trackingProcedure: Track application and test rank on shreshta.nta.nic.in using application number.

disbursementMethod: Direct payment from Ministry of Social Justice to CBSE Residential School
disbursementDetails: Tuition fee, hostel charges, mess bill, and stationery allowance disbursed directly to the school account.

faqs.q: Is there any exam fee for NETS?
faqs.a: No. The National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA is 100% free with zero application fee.

faqs.q: Which schools can students study in?
faqs.a: Top-ranking private residential schools affiliated to CBSE identified by the Ministry based on academic performance.

name: PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM-YASASVI)
title: PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM-YASASVI)
department: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice
targetBeneficiary: Other Backward Class (OBC), Economically Backward Class (EBC), and De-Notified Tribe (DNT) students in Classes 9 to 12
description: Pre-matric and Top-Class school scholarship providing ₹75,000/year (Class 9-10) and ₹1,25,000/year (Class 11-12) to meritorious OBC, EBC, and DNT students studying in identified top schools.
detailedDescription: PM-YASASVI is a premier umbrella scholarship for marginalized Other Backward Classes (OBC), Economically Backward Classes (EBC), and Nomadic/De-Notified Tribes (DNT). It offers Top-Class School Education scholarships of ₹75,000 per annum for Class 9 and 10 students, and ₹1,25,000 per annum for Class 11 and 12 students admitted to identified top-performing schools across India. Funds are credited straight into the student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account via the National Scholarship Portal (NSP).
purpose: Promotes educational excellence and prevents dropouts among disadvantaged backward class students, supporting SDG 4 and SDG 10.
benefits: Direct scholarship of ₹75,000 per year for Class 9-10 and ₹1,25,000 per year for Class 11-12 covering tuition fee, hostel charges, books, and computer equipment.
financialBenefit: ₹75,000/year (Class 9-10) or ₹1,25,000/year (Class 11-12) via DBT
benefitFrequency: Annual recurring scholarship
impact: Over 3.5 lakh OBC/EBC/DNT students supported annually, enabling top high school completion.
specificAdvantages: Direct scholarship credit via PFMS without state intermediary delays.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Annual parental income not exceeding ₹2,50,000.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Studying in Class 9, 10, 11, or 12 in an identified top school.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: OBC, EBC, or DNT/SNT categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Family income within benchmark.

mandatoryConditions: Must belong to OBC, EBC, or DNT category with valid community certificate
Annual family income must not exceed ₹2.5 Lakh per year
Must be studying in an identified top school listed on the National Scholarship Portal
ineligibility: Students receiving other central scholarship grants
Family income exceeding ₹2.5 Lakh/year

documents.name: OBC / EBC / DNT Caste Certificate
documents.why: Community eligibility proof.

documents.name: Income Certificate (Below ₹2.5 Lakh)
documents.why: Confirms income limit.

documents.name: Previous Year Marksheet (Minimum 60% marks)
documents.why: Academic merit proof.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Linked Bank Account
documents.why: For DBT scholarship transfer.

applicationMode: Online via National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in)
process: Step 1: Visit scholarships.gov.in and register with One-Time Registration (OTR).
Step 2: Under Ministry of Social Justice schemes, select 'PM-YASASVI Top Class School Education'.
Step 3: Enter academic records, caste certificate, and income details.
Step 4: School verifies student details on the NSP portal.
Step 5: District Nodal Officer (DNO) and Ministry approve the merit list.
Step 6: Scholarship amount (₹75,000 or ₹1,25,000) is credited directly via PFMS DBT.
offlineProcess: Apply online on NSP. School nodal officer assists students with online portal submission.
commonMistakes: Applying for a school that is not on the Ministry's identified top school roster.
Bank account not active or not in the student's name.

renewalRequired: Annual renewal on NSP upon promotion to subsequent class

correctionProcedure: Request school verification officer to mark application for correction on NSP.

disbursementDetails: Funds transferred electronically through PFMS into the student's Aadhaar-linked savings account.

faqs.q: Is an entrance exam compulsory?
faqs.a: Selection for top schools is based on Class 8 or Class 10 academic merit scores and merit lists prepared on the National Scholarship Portal.

name: NAMASTE Scheme (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem)
title: NAMASTE Scheme (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem)
department: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs & Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
stateCoverage: All 4,800+ Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across India
targetBeneficiary: Sewer and septic tank sanitation workers (SSWs) and manual scavengers
description: Mission to achieve zero fatalities in sanitation work by providing sewer workers with free PPE safety gear, mechanised cleaning machine capital subsidies up to ₹5 Lakh, and Ayushman Bharat health insurance.
detailedDescription: The NAMASTE Scheme is a joint national initiative to eliminate hazardous manual entry into sewers and septic tanks. Every identified sewer and septic tank worker receives free digital profiling (NAMASTE photo ID card), free PPE kits with gas detectors, free Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY health insurance cards, and skill training with a ₹3,000 stipend. To turn sewer workers into sanitation entrepreneurs ('Sanipreneurs'), the government provides up to 50% capital subsidy (up to ₹5,00,000) for procuring modern mechanised desilting machines and sewer vacuum trucks.
purpose: Achieves zero sanitation fatalities, eradicates hazardous manual scavenging, and provides economic dignity and mechanized equipment to sanitation workers, supporting SDG 3, SDG 6, and SDG 8.
benefits: Free Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) safety kit, free Ayushman Bharat health insurance, certified skill training with ₹3,000 stipend, and up to ₹5,00,000 capital subsidy for purchasing sewer cleaning machines.
financialBenefit: Capital subsidy up to ₹5,00,000 for sewer machines + Free ₹5 Lakh health cover + Free PPE kits
benefitFrequency: One-time asset subsidy + Annual health insurance coverage
impact: Over 85,000 sewer workers profiled; hazardous entry deaths curtailed through complete machine-led desilting.
specificAdvantages: Transforms manual scavengers into mechanized contractors ('Sanipreneurs') with guaranteed urban municipal contracts.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Sewer and septic tank worker / sanitation worker.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (majority SC/ST workers).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Identified during Urban Local Body (ULB) sanitation worker profiling.

mandatoryConditions: Must be engaged in sewer or septic tank cleaning work verified by the local Urban Local Body (ULB)
Must participate in the NAMASTE profiling survey and receive a NAMASTE ID card
For machinery loans, must form a group or register as an enterprise under NSKFDC
ineligibility: Non-sanitation workers

documents.name: NAMASTE Worker ID Card / ULB Verification Certificate
documents.why: Proof of sewer/sanitation work.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card & Bank Account Passbook
documents.why: Identity and DBT subsidy credit.

documents.name: Quotation for Mechanised Sewer Cleaning Equipment
documents.why: Required for claiming capital machine subsidy.

applicationMode: Profiling through local Municipal Corporation / ULB & Online via namaste.gov.in
process: Step 1: Participate in the NAMASTE mobile profiling camp conducted by your local Municipal Corporation.
Step 2: Provide your biometric Aadhaar and photograph to receive your NAMASTE Sanitation Worker ID Card.
Step 3: Collect your free PPE safety equipment kit and Ayushman Bharat health card.
Step 4: Attend the 3-day mechanized sanitation safety training and receive ₹3,000 stipend.
Step 5: If applying to buy a desilting machine/suction truck, submit project proposal to National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
Step 6: Bank sanctions machine loan; government credits up to ₹5 Lakh capital subsidy directly to the vendor.
offlineProcess: Meet the Health Officer / Sanitary Inspector at your Municipal Corporation or Municipality office.
commonMistakes: Cleaning sewers without the mandatory PPE gas-detector kit (strictly penalized under law).
Not registering during the Urban Local Body profiling drive.
openingDate: Continuous profiling active across all Indian cities and towns
processingTime: Immediate profiling and kit handover; machinery loans approved in 30 days
renewalRequired: Safety equipment kits replaced every 2 years
trackingProcedure: Track worker ID on namaste.gov.in or inquire at the Municipal Corporation health section.
correctionProcedure: Contact Municipal Nodal Officer for NAMASTE.
disbursementMethod: Direct asset delivery (PPE kits) + DBT subsidy to machine manufacturer / loan account
disbursementDetails: Safety gear distributed directly; capital machine subsidies credited to the lending bank account via NSKFDC.

faqs.q: Is manual entry into sewers allowed?
faqs.a: No. Hazardous manual entry is strictly illegal under the MS Act 2013; all cleaning must be 100% mechanized under NAMASTE.

name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
department: Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)
targetBeneficiary: Poor rural youth aged 15-35 from MGNREGA, BPL, and Antyodaya households
description: Placement-linked residential skill training program for rural poor youth guaranteeing minimum 70% job placement in formal private sector companies with monthly salaries.
detailedDescription: DDU-GKY is a market-led, placement-linked skill initiative under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM). It trains rural poor youth in demand-driven skills (hospitality, retail, healthcare, logistics, electronics, automotive, BPO) through fully residential training centres. Training, boarding, lodging, uniforms, books, and tablets are 100% free. The scheme mandates that training partners must place at least 70% of certified candidates into formal jobs with wages above minimum statutory benchmarks, followed by 6 months of post-placement retention support.
purpose: Transforms rural youth from subsistence labor into productive formal economic contributors, bridging the rural-urban wage divide, supporting SDG 1 and SDG 8.
benefits: 100% free residential training with boarding and lodging, free uniforms, tablets, study materials, recognized national certification, and guaranteed job placement with post-placement financial support.
financialBenefit: Free residential training worth ₹35,000 to ₹70,000 per youth + Monthly post-placement allowance
benefitFrequency: One-time residential training course (3 to 12 months duration)
impact: Over 14 lakh rural youth trained and placed in corporate jobs, creating sustainable remittances for rural poor families.
specificAdvantages: Mandatory 70% corporate placement guarantee; residential boarding eliminates rural commuting difficulties.

detailedEligibility.ageRequirement: 15 to 35 years (up to 45 years for Women, SC/ST, Persons with Disabilities, Transgender).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Must belong to rural poor families (MGNREGA household with 15+ days work, BPL, SECC, or RSBY).
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Minimum Class 5 pass up to 12th/Graduate depending on job role.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories (minimum 50% SC/ST, 15% Minorities).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Member of a verified rural poor household.

mandatoryConditions: Must be a rural resident aged between 15 and 35 years
Family must be identified under rural deprivation criteria (MGNREGA job card, BPL card, or SHG member family)
Must commit to full-time residential training and relocation for formal corporate employment
ineligibility: Urban residents
Youth already placed in formal sector jobs with active PF accounts

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Mandatory biometric identification.

documents.name: Rural Poor Proof (MGNREGA Job Card / BPL Ration Card / SECC / SHG Letter)
documents.why: Confirms rural poor status.

documents.name: Educational Certificate / Marksheet
documents.why: Qualifies for specific sector trade.

documents.name: Bank Account Passbook
documents.why: For receiving post-placement retention allowance.

applicationMode: Online via Kaushal Panjee (kaushalpanjee.nic.in) & Offline at Block Development Office / Rozgar Melas
process: Step 1: Register on kaushalpanjee.nic.in using your mobile number and Aadhaar.
Step 2: Attend the local Mobilization Camp or Rozgar Mela organized by the State Rural Livelihood Mission (SRLM).
Step 3: Undergo career counseling and choose your training sector (e.g. Retail, IT-BPO, Healthcare, Hospitality).
Step 4: Join the accredited residential training centre with 100% free food and accommodation.
Step 5: Complete technical, computer, and soft-skill English communication training.
Step 6: Attend campus recruitment interviews and join your formal corporate employer.
offlineProcess: Meet the Block Mission Manager (NRLM) at your local Block Development Office (BDO) or attend village mobilization camps.
commonMistakes: Leaving the residential training midway before completing assessment.
Providing an urban address (DDU-GKY is exclusively for rural residents).
openingDate: Continuous enrollment with monthly new residential batches
processingTime: Course duration spans 3 to 12 months depending on trade
renewalRequired: One-time training; post-placement tracking for 6 to 12 months
trackingProcedure: Track candidate progress on ddugky.gov.in using candidate PRN number.
correctionProcedure: Contact Project Implementing Agency (PIA) centre coordinator.
disbursementMethod: Direct training and boarding funding to training partner + DBT post-placement support to youth
disbursementDetails: Training and boarding costs funded by Ministry of Rural Development; monthly post-placement allowance credited directly via DBT to candidate.

faqs.q: Is boarding and food completely free?
faqs.a: Yes. Food, AC/clean hostel accommodation, uniforms, and learning materials are 100% free.

faqs.q: What is the post-placement allowance?
faqs.a: Candidates placed within their home district receive ₹1,000/month for 2 months; placed outside district: ₹1,000/month for 3 months; placed outside state: ₹1,000/month for 6 months.

name: National Career Service (NCS)
title: National Career Service (NCS)
department: Ministry of Labour and Employment
targetBeneficiary: All job seekers, fresh graduates, skilled professionals, and gig workers
description: National employment exchange digital platform connecting over 3.5 crore job seekers with 38 lakh verified employers, offering free job listings, career counseling, and job melas.
detailedDescription: National Career Service (NCS) is India's official public employment platform, modernizing erstwhile physical employment exchanges into a nationwide digital ecosystem. Job seekers access thousands of verified active vacancies in Central Government, State Governments, public sector undertakings, and leading private corporate enterprises with zero fees. The platform integrates career counseling, psychometric aptitude testing, free vocational courses via Microsoft and TCS iON, and regular online/offline Job Fairs (Rozgar Melas) in every district.
purpose: Connects employers and job seekers on a verified, transparent, fee-free national platform, eliminating fraudulent recruitment agencies and advancing SDG 8.
benefits: Free job application across thousands of public and private vacancies, verified employer profiles, free career counseling, psychometric assessments, digital employment cards, and job mela participation.
financialBenefit: 100% Free career matchmaking, counseling, and interview scheduling (Zero recruitment fee)
benefitFrequency: Continuous ongoing service
impact: Over 3.5 crore registered job seekers; millions of verified placements facilitated across healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, IT, banking, and public sectors.
specificAdvantages: Completely scam-free and verified by the Ministry of Labour; integrated with DigiLocker and e-Shram portals.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: All qualification levels (from literate, Class 10, Diploma, up to Ph.D.).
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Any job seeker (freshers, experienced, gig workers).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: None.

mandatoryConditions: Must register on the NCS portal (ncs.gov.in) with valid Aadhaar or government photo ID
Completion of candidate profile with educational qualifications and skills
ineligibility: Fraudulent candidate profiles

documents.name: Government Photo ID (Aadhaar / PAN / Voter ID)
documents.why: Identity verification.

documents.name: Resume / Curriculum Vitae
documents.why: Specifies work experience and skills.

documents.name: Educational Marksheets & Degrees
documents.why: Verification of educational qualifications.

applicationMode: 100% Online via ncs.gov.in & Offline at Model Career Centres (MCC)
process: Step 1: Visit ncs.gov.in and click 'Jobseeker' > 'Register'.
Step 2: Enter Aadhaar / PAN for instant e-KYC authentication.
Step 3: Complete your educational history, technical skills, and preferred work locations.
Step 4: Download your official National Career Service (NCS) Jobseeker ID Card.
Step 5: Search and filter thousands of verified active vacancies by state, salary, and job role.
Step 6: Apply with one click; verified employers contact you directly for interview schedules.
offlineProcess: Walk into any Model Career Centre (MCC) or District Employment Exchange across India for in-person counseling and offline job mela registration.
commonMistakes: Paying fees to unauthorized third-party job agents (NCS and government job applications are strictly 100% free under law).
Not updating skills and mobile numbers on the candidate profile.
processingTime: Instant registration and immediate job application
renewalRequired: Profile remains active; periodic updates recommended
trackingProcedure: Track applied jobs and interview invitations in the 'Candidate Dashboard' on ncs.gov.in.
correctionProcedure: Edit candidate profile directly on ncs.gov.in.
disbursementMethod: Direct employer-to-candidate recruitment matching
disbursementDetails: Employers schedule online or in-person interviews; successful candidates receive direct employment offer letters.

faqs.q: Is there any charge to register or apply for jobs on NCS?
faqs.a: No. National Career Service is 100% free for both job seekers and employers.

faqs.q: Are government jobs listed on NCS?
faqs.a: Yes. Major Central Ministries, State Departments, and PSUs list their official recruitment openings on NCS.

helpline: NCS National Toll-Free Helpline: 1514 (Available Tuesday to Sunday, 8 AM - 8 PM)

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture
targetBeneficiary: Farmers cultivating in clusters adopting chemical-free traditional organic farming
description: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare over 3 years (₹31,000 direct DBT to farmer for organic inputs + ₹19,000 for PGS organic certification, packaging, and marketing).
detailedDescription: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) promotes traditional, sustainable, and chemical-free organic farming across India. Implemented on a cluster basis (clusters of 20 or more farmers holding 20 hectares combined), the government provides financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare over 3 years. ₹31,000 per hectare is transferred directly to the farmer via DBT for organic seeds, bio-fertilizers, vermicompost, and botanical extracts. The remaining ₹19,000 covers free Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) organic certification, testing, and marketing on the Jaivik Kheti e-commerce portal.
purpose: Restores soil biological fertility, eliminates dangerous chemical pesticide residues, lowers cultivation costs for dryland farmers, and opens premium organic market prices, supporting SDG 2 and SDG 12.
benefits: Direct financial assistance of ₹31,000/ha for organic inputs + free PGS-India organic certification + free soil testing + direct onboarding to the Jaivik Kheti national marketplace.
financialBenefit: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare over 3 years (₹31,000 direct DBT to farmer)
benefitFrequency: Annual phased installments over 3-year organic conversion cycle
impact: Over 12 lakh hectares certified under zero-budget natural and organic farming, raising net farmer profits by 20-30% through organic price premiums.
specificAdvantages: Zero certification charges under PGS-India; farmer-to-consumer direct selling without middlemen on jaivikkheti.in.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Must join or form a local farmer cluster of minimum 20 farmers (20 hectares).

mandatoryConditions: Must own or cultivate agricultural land within an identified 20-hectare organic farming cluster
Must commit to complete stoppage of synthetic chemical fertilizers and chemical pesticides
Must adopt Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) peer inspection protocols
ineligibility: Individual scattered farm plots not part of any recognized farming cluster
Farms continuing chemical pesticide applications

documents.name: Agricultural Land Records (RTC / Khasra / Khatauni)
documents.why: Proof of land acreage and survey boundary.

documents.name: Aadhaar Card
documents.why: Farmer identification and e-KYC.

documents.name: Aadhaar-Linked Bank Passbook
documents.why: For receiving ₹31,000/ha DBT organic input grant.

applicationMode: Cluster Formation via Block Agriculture Office & Online via pgsindia-ncof.gov.in
process: Step 1: Form a group of 20 or more interested farmers holding 20 hectares contiguous farmland in your village.
Step 2: Approach your Block Agriculture Officer (BAO) or District Horticulture Officer.
Step 3: Register the cluster under the Participatory Guarantee System on pgsindia-ncof.gov.in.
Step 4: Regional Council approves the cluster and registers farmers.
Step 5: First installment of input subsidy is transferred directly via DBT to each farmer's bank account.
Step 6: Follow organic protocols, undergo peer inspection, receive green PGS organic certification, and sell on jaivikkheti.in.
offlineProcess: Meet your local Agriculture Extension Officer or Raitha Samparka Kendra / Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
commonMistakes: Applying individually without forming a cluster (minimum 20 farmers holding 20 ha is required).
Using non-approved synthetic weedicides during the 3-year conversion period.
openingDate: Continuous cluster sanctioning throughout the financial year
processingTime: Cluster approved in 30 days; 3-year phased organic certification
renewalRequired: Annual PGS peer review certification
trackingProcedure: Track cluster and farmer certification status on pgsindia-ncof.gov.in by entering state and district.
correctionProcedure: Contact Regional Council nodal agency for cluster updates.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Farmer Bank Account + Certification Grants
disbursementDetails: Input subsidy credited directly into the farmer's bank account via PFMS across 3 years. Certification and testing expenses settled by the state nodal agency.

faqs.q: What is the PGS-India organic certificate?
faqs.a: A decentralized organic certification recognized by FSSAI for domestic organic food sales, operated at zero cost to farmers.

faqs.q: Where can farmers sell their organic produce?
faqs.a: Directly on the Government Jaivik Kheti e-commerce portal (jaivikkheti.in) or at local organic mandis at premium prices.

helpline: National Centre of Organic Farming (NCOF): 0120-2764906 / Kisan Helpline: 1800-180-1551

name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
title: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
department: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
stateCoverage: All 28 States & 8 Union Territories (Marine and Inland)
targetBeneficiary: Fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, fisheries cooperatives, and entrepreneurs
description: Flagship fisheries and aquaculture scheme with ₹20,050 Crore outlay providing 40% to 60% government subsidy for fish ponds, biofloc units, RAS, deep-sea fishing vessels, and cold storage.
detailedDescription: PMMSY is the highest-ever investment in Indian fisheries history. It modernizes marine and inland aquaculture by offering 40% government subsidy (for General category) and 60% government subsidy (for SC, ST, and Women beneficiaries) on a wide spectrum of fisheries projects. Covered activities include new freshwater/saline fish and shrimp pond construction, Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), Biofloc units, modern fishing boats, marine cages, insulated fish vans, live fish retail kiosks, and ice plants.
purpose: Drives the Blue Revolution, doubles fishers' incomes, cuts post-harvest marine losses from 20% to under 10%, and boosts seafood exports, supporting SDG 1, SDG 8, and SDG 14.
benefits: Direct capital subsidy of 40% (General) to 60% (Women / SC / ST) on project costs ranging from ₹50,000 (small fish retail kiosk) up to ₹50,00,000+ (commercial RAS/biofloc units and deep-sea vessels).
financialBenefit: 40% to 60% capital subsidy on commercial fisheries and aquaculture projects
benefitFrequency: Milestone-based project capital subsidy
impact: Fish production has surged past 175 lakh tonnes; over 55 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities generated across coastal and inland regions.
specificAdvantages: Women entrepreneurs and SC/ST farmers receive an enhanced 60% subsidy; covers both small backyard ponds and large export processing facilities.

detailedEligibility.genderRequirement: All genders eligible (women receive enhanced 60% subsidy).
detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: No income limit.
detailedEligibility.occupationRequirement: Fisher, fish farmer, self-help group, or fisheries entrepreneur.
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all (60% subsidy for SC/ST/Women; 40% for General/OBC men).
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Must own or hold on lease suitable land or water body for the project period (minimum 7 years for land lease).

mandatoryConditions: Must have land/water body ownership documents or registered long-term lease agreement (minimum 7 to 10 years)
Must contribute minimum 40% to 60% balance project cost through personal equity or bank loan
Detailed Project Report (DPR) approved by the District Fisheries Development Officer
ineligibility: Projects without registered land/water access
Applicants defaulting on earlier fisheries corporation loans

documents.name: Land / Waterbody Ownership Document or Registered Lease Deed
documents.why: Proof of site where aquaculture pond / RAS / biofloc unit will be built.

documents.name: Detailed Project Report (DPR) with Technical Estimates
documents.why: Specifies engineering civil work, aerators, seed, feed, and capital costs.

documents.name: Caste Certificate (for SC/ST) & Gender Proof
documents.why: Determines 60% subsidy eligibility.

documents.name: Bank Passbook & Consent Letter from Bank (for loan component)
documents.why: For subsidy disbursement.

applicationMode: Online via pmmsy.dof.gov.in & Offline through District Fisheries Office
process: Step 1: Choose an eligible fisheries activity (e.g. Biofloc, RAS, pond excavation, ice plant, motorcycle with icebox).
Step 2: Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) with certified quotations for equipment.
Step 3: Register and submit application on pmmsy.dof.gov.in.
Step 4: District Level Committee (DLC) headed by the District Magistrate scrutinizes the proposal.
Step 5: State Fisheries Directorate sanctions administrative approval.
Step 6: Construct the unit / buy equipment; Fisheries officer inspects site and releases subsidy in installments via DBT.
offlineProcess: Submit application at the office of the Assistant Director / District Fisheries Development Officer in your district headquarters.
commonMistakes: Commencing civil construction before receiving formal administrative approval from the Fisheries Department.
Submitting an unregistered lease agreement (lease MUST be registered at the Sub-Registrar office).
openingDate: Continuous year-round portal window with quarterly DLC review meetings
processingTime: 45 to 60 business days from DLC submission to sanction
renewalRequired: One-time project capital subsidy
trackingProcedure: Track application status on pmmsy.dof.gov.in using application number.
correctionProcedure: Revise DPR or lease documents as directed by the District Fisheries Officer.
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Beneficiary Bank Account / Bank Subsidy Reserve
disbursementDetails: Disbursed in 2 to 3 milestone installments: 1st after initial civil work, 2nd after equipment installation, 3rd after physical geo-tagged inspection.

faqs.q: Can women entrepreneurs apply for 60% subsidy?
faqs.a: Yes. All individual women applicants and women SHGs/cooperatives receive the enhanced 60% government subsidy.

faqs.q: What is the subsidy for a motorcycle with an insulated ice box?

name: Mission Vatsalya (Child Protection and Sponsorship Scheme)
title: Mission Vatsalya (Child Protection and Sponsorship Scheme)
department: Ministry of Women and Child Development
targetBeneficiary: Children in difficult circumstances: orphans, children of single/destitute parents, child survivors, and children at risk of dropping out
description: Monthly financial sponsorship of ₹4,000 per child transferred directly via DBT to destitute single parents, foster families, or kin to keep vulnerable children in family care and schooling.
detailedDescription: Mission Vatsalya (formerly Child Protection Services / ICPS) provides non-institutional family-based care to children in need of care and protection. Under its Family-Based Sponsorship component, the government deposits ₹4,000 per month per child directly into the bank account of a widowed mother, divorced mother, single destitute parent, or kinship caregiver. This ensures the child is not abandoned into child care institutions or forced into child labor, and can continue regular schooling.
purpose: Prevents family separation, child labor, and institutionalization by providing direct financial survival grants to kinship caregivers, supporting SDG 1, SDG 4, and SDG 10.
benefits: Direct financial cash assistance of ₹4,000 per child per month transferred via DBT, plus complete child protection, counseling, and school enrollment assistance.
financialBenefit: ₹4,00,0 per child per month (₹48,000 per year) direct cash sponsorship
benefitFrequency: Monthly Direct Benefit Transfer until child attains 18 years of age
impact: Over 1.8 lakh destitute children shielded from orphanages and street begging, enabling them to grow within their biological families with dignity.
specificAdvantages: Money paid straight to biological mother/caregiver; allows children to stay in their own homes instead of institutional orphanages.

detailedEligibility.incomeLimit: Family annual income up to ₹72,000 (rural) or ₹96,000 (urban).
detailedEligibility.educationRequirement: Must be enrolled in school (regular attendance required).
detailedEligibility.casteCategoryRequirement: Open to all categories.
detailedEligibility.familyConditions: Child of a widow, divorced/abandoned mother, parents suffering from terminal illness, or orphan living with grandparents/kin.

ineligibility: Families whose annual income exceeds ₹96,000
Children who drop out of school without medical justification

applicationMode: Offline submission at District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) / Child Welfare Committee (CWC)
process: Step 1: Obtain the Mission Vatsalya Sponsorship application proforma from your District Child Protection Unit (DCPU).
Step 2: Attach child birth proof, school study certificate, death certificate of father (if widowed), and income proof.
Step 3: District Child Protection Officer (DCPO) conducts a social home investigation.
Step 4: The Sponsorship and Foster Care Approval Committee (SFCAC) chaired by the District Magistrate / CWC approves the case.
Step 5: ₹4,000 per month is deposited via DBT directly into the mother's / guardian's joint bank account.
Step 6: Submit annual school progress report to maintain uninterrupted monthly sponsorship.
offlineProcess: Visit the District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) located in the District Collectorate / Social Welfare complex in your district.
commonMistakes: Child dropping out of school (school attendance is mandatory to receive monthly sponsorship).
Applying without an income certificate.
processingTime: 30 to 45 business days for CWC and DCPU inquiry and sanction
renewalRequired: Annual review by CWC based on school progress report
trackingProcedure: Inquire at the District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) with your application registration number.
correctionProcedure: Contact District Child Protection Officer (DCPO).
disbursementMethod: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Joint Bank Account (Parent/Guardian & Child)
disbursementDetails: ₹4,000 per month deposited via state treasury electronic DBT into the beneficiary's bank account on the first week of every month.

faqs.q: How many children per family can receive sponsorship?
faqs.a: Maximum two children per family can receive the ₹4,000/month sponsorship grant.

faqs.q: What happens when the child turns 18?
faqs.a: Sponsorship ceases at age 18; youth can then transition to the Aftercare Financial Support program up to age 21.
